```{r}
#| label: laminar-table

lam_long <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) qnp_raw[[r]] %>%
  filter(`analysis region` %in% c("Grey matter", LAM_LAYERS)) %>%
  transmute(donor_id = `Donor ID`, brain_region = `brain region`, analysis_region = `analysis region`,
            at8 = .data[[LAM_AT8]], neun = .data[[LAM_NEUN]] * 1e6))
lam_gm <- lam_long %>% filter(analysis_region == "Grey matter") %>%
  select(donor_id, brain_region, at8_gm = at8, neun_gm = neun) %>%
  group_by(brain_region) %>%
  mutate(burden = log2(at8_gm + LAM_LOG_OFFSET), at8_gm_ns = normal_score(at8_gm)) %>% ungroup()

lay <- lam_long %>% filter(analysis_region %in% LAM_LAYERS) %>%
  mutate(layer = factor(analysis_region, levels = LAM_LAYERS)) %>%
  left_join(lam_gm, by = c("donor_id", "brain_region")) %>%
  left_join(donor %>% select(donor_id, CPS_Global_pTau, gp_tertile, severe, is_act), by = "donor_id") %>%
  mutate(y = log2(at8 + LAM_LOG_OFFSET),
         D = y - burden) %>%                                   # log2 enrichment relative to the region
  group_by(brain_region, layer) %>%
  mutate(P = D - mean(D),                                     # minus the cohort's typical laminar profile
         at8_ns = normal_score(at8), neun_ns = normal_score(neun)) %>%
  group_by(brain_region, donor_id) %>%
  mutate(clr = y - mean(y),                                   # within-donor sum-to-zero profile
         at8_w = at8_ns - mean(at8_ns)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(donor %>% transmute(donor_id, gz = zstd(CPS_Global_pTau)), by = "donor_id") %>%   # SD over the 84 donors
  mutate(brain_region = factor(brain_region, levels = LAM_REGIONS)) %>%
  arrange(brain_region, donor_id, layer)

# Is the whole-region value an aggregate of the same layers? (No area-analysed column is
# released, so check it empirically: grey matter on the five layers, no intercept.)
lam_gm_check <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) map_dfr(c(AT8 = "at8", NeuN = "neun"), function(v) {
  w <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% select(donor_id, layer, val = all_of(v)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = val) %>%
    left_join(lam_gm %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% select(donor_id, gm = all_of(paste0(v, "_gm"))), by = "donor_id")
  L <- as.matrix(w[LAM_LAYERS]); f <- lm(w$gm ~ 0 + L)
  tibble(Region = r, Stain = v, weights = paste(sprintf("%.2f", coef(f)), collapse = " / "),
         weight_sum = sum(coef(f)), r2 = summary(f)$r.squared,
         inside = mean(w$gm >= apply(L, 1, min) & w$gm <= apply(L, 1, max)))
}, .id = "stain_label"))
stopifnot(
  "one row per donor x region x layer, every layer for every donor" =
    !anyDuplicated(lay[c("donor_id", "brain_region", "layer")]) && all(count(lay, brain_region, donor_id)$n == 5),
  "all 84 donors in each eligible region" = all(count(distinct(lay, brain_region, donor_id), brain_region)$n == 84L),
  "no missing or zero layer AT8 / NeuN value" = !anyNA(lay[c("at8", "neun", "at8_gm", "neun_gm")]) && all(lay$at8 > 0),
  "grey matter is an area-weighted aggregate of the five layers" =
    all(abs(lam_gm_check$weight_sum - 1) < 0.03) && all(lam_gm_check$r2 > 0.99) && all(lam_gm_check$inside == 1),
  "the relative profile is centred within each layer" = all(abs(tapply(lay$P, list(lay$brain_region, lay$layer), mean)) < 1e-10),
  "the clr profile sums to zero within donor" = all(abs(tapply(lay$clr, paste(lay$brain_region, lay$donor_id), sum)) < 1e-10)
)
lam_gm_check %>% transmute(Region, Stain = stain_label,
                           `Fitted layer weights (L1 / L2 / L3 / L4 / L5–6)` = weights,
                           `Sum of weights` = weight_sum, `R²` = r2,
                           `Grey matter inside layer range` = percent(inside)) %>%
  show_table(digits = 4, caption = "Grey matter regressed on the five layer values (no intercept), per region and stain. Weights summing to 1 with R² ≈ 1 and grey matter always inside the layer range identify the released grey-matter value as an area-weighted aggregate of the same layer measurements.")
```

```{r}
#| label: laminar-area-weights

# Are explicit per-donor layer areas released anywhere? The June region tabs drop the
# documented "area analyzed" columns; only the deprecated Gabitto MTG tab keeps them.
area_sheets <- names(qnp_raw)[map_lgl(qnp_raw, ~ any(str_detect(names(.x), "area analyzed")))]
gab_area <- map_dfr(c(LAM_LAYERS, "Grey matter"), function(l) tibble(
  donor_id = gab$`Donor ID`, analysis_region = l,
  at8_gab = gab[[paste0(LAM_AT8, "_", l)]],
  area = gab[[paste0("AT8 and pTDP43 area analyzed_", l)]]))
lam_area <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == "MTG") %>% select(donor_id, layer, at8, gz) %>%
  mutate(analysis_region = as.character(layer)) %>%
  left_join(gab_area, by = c("donor_id", "analysis_region")) %>%
  group_by(donor_id) %>% mutate(area_share = area / sum(area)) %>% ungroup()
gab_gm <- gab_area %>% filter(analysis_region == "Grey matter")
lam_area_gm <- lam_area %>% group_by(donor_id) %>%
  summarise(area_sum = sum(area), at8_aw = sum(area * at8) / sum(area), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(gab_gm %>% select(donor_id, area_gm = area, at8_gm_gab = at8_gab), by = "donor_id")
stopifnot(
  "explicit layer areas exist only in the deprecated Gabitto MTG tab" =
    identical(area_sheets, "Gabitto 2024 (deprecated; MTG)"),
  "the deprecated tab's layer AT8 is identical to the June MTG layer AT8" =
    nrow(lam_area) == 420L && !anyNA(lam_area$area) && max(abs(lam_area$at8 - lam_area$at8_gab)) < 1e-9,
  "MTG layer areas sum to the grey-matter area and reproduce grey-matter AT8 exactly" =
    max(abs(lam_area_gm$area_sum / lam_area_gm$area_gm - 1)) < 1e-6 &&
    max(abs(lam_area_gm$at8_aw - lam_area_gm$at8_gm_gab)) < 1e-6
)
# Does the registered layer geometry itself vary with progression? (MTG only; areas are
# the NeuN-classifier layer bins propagated to the AT8 slide.)
area_w <- lam_area %>% select(donor_id, layer, area_share, gz) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = area_share)
lam_area_gz <- tibble(layer = LAM_LAYERS,
                      mean_share = colMeans(area_w[LAM_LAYERS]),
                      rho = map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, ~ cor(area_w[[.x]], area_w$gz, method = "spearman")))
lam_area_gz_p <- anova(lm(as.matrix(area_w[LAM_LAYERS[1:4]]) ~ area_w$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2]
lam_area_gz %>% transmute(Layer = LAM_LAB[layer], `Mean share of analysed MTG grey-matter area` = percent(mean_share, 0.1),
                          `Spearman ρ with Global pTau` = sprintf("%+.2f", rho)) %>%
  show_table(caption = sprintf("MTG layer areas from the deprecated Gabitto tab (AT8/pTDP-43 slide). Joint test that the layer-area composition changes with Global pTau (Pillai, 4 shares): p = %s. DFC has no released layer areas.", format(lam_area_gz_p, digits = 2)))

# Every stain slide carries its own released layer areas (same registered annotation, different
# section). Classifier-derived layer-area fractions per slide, against continuous Global pTau.
MTG_AREA_SLIDES <- c("AT8 and pTDP43", "Iba1 and 6e10", "GFAP", "NeuN", "Hematoxylin")
mtg_area <- map_dfr(MTG_AREA_SLIDES, function(sl) map_dfr(LAM_LAYERS, function(l) tibble(
  donor_id = gab$`Donor ID`, slide = sl, layer = factor(l, levels = LAM_LAYERS),
  area = gab[[paste0(sl, " area analyzed_", l)]], area_gm = gab[[paste0(sl, " area analyzed_Grey matter")]]))) %>%
  group_by(slide, donor_id) %>% mutate(frac = area / sum(area)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  left_join(donor %>% transmute(donor_id, gz = zstd(CPS_Global_pTau)), by = "donor_id")
stopifnot(
  "layer areas come only from released 'area analyzed' columns of the MTG deprecated tab, never DFC" =
    all(paste0(rep(MTG_AREA_SLIDES, each = 6), " area analyzed_", c(LAM_LAYERS, "Grey matter")) %in% names(gab)) &&
    !any(str_detect(names(qnp_raw[["DFC"]]), "area analyzed")),
  "every slide's five layer areas are complete and sum to its grey-matter area" =
    !anyNA(mtg_area$area) && all(mtg_area$area > 0) &&
    max(abs(mtg_area %>% group_by(slide, donor_id) %>% summarise(r = sum(area) / first(area_gm), .groups = "drop") %>% pull(r) - 1)) < 1e-6
)
lam_geom <- mtg_area %>% group_by(slide) %>% group_modify(function(d, key) {
  w <- d %>% select(donor_id, layer, frac, gz) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = frac)
  tibble(layer = LAM_LAYERS, mean_frac = colMeans(w[LAM_LAYERS]),
         slope = map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, ~ unname(coef(lm(w[[.x]] ~ w$gz))[2])),
         std = map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, ~ cor(w[[.x]], w$gz)),
         p = anova(lm(as.matrix(w[LAM_LAYERS[1:4]]) ~ w$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2])
}) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(slide = factor(slide, levels = MTG_AREA_SLIDES))
lgeo <- function(sl, l, col = "std") lam_geom[[col]][lam_geom$slide == sl & lam_geom$layer == l]
stopifnot("the L3-down / L4-up geometry shift is present on every stain slide (as stated)" =
            all(lam_geom$std[lam_geom$layer == "Layer3"] < 0) && all(lam_geom$std[lam_geom$layer == "Layer4"] > 0))
write_csv(lam_geom, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_MTG_layer_geometry.csv"))
```

**Layer-area weights.** The June 2026 region tabs omit the documented `area analyzed` columns.
They survive only in the deprecated Gabitto MTG tab, whose layer AT8 values are **identical** to
the June MTG layers, whose layer areas sum exactly to the grey-matter area, and whose
area-weighted layer mean reproduces grey-matter AT8 exactly. So:

- **MTG:** explicit, per-donor layer-area weights exist and are reliable.
- **DFC:** no layer areas are released. They are not inferred by solving backwards from the AT8
  values.
- **The layer geometry is not fixed.** In MTG the share of analysed area assigned to each layer
  varies between donors (L1 `r sprintf("%.0f–%.0f%%", 100 * min(area_w$Layer1), 100 * max(area_w$Layer1))`)
  and shifts with progression (p `r format(lam_area_gz_p, digits = 2)`; L3 share
  `r sprintf("%+.2f", lam_area_gz$rho[3])`, L4 `r sprintf("%+.2f", lam_area_gz$rho[4])` Spearman ρ
  with Global pTau). The same L3-down, L4-up shift appears on all five stain slides
  (Supplementary Figure S5A), as expected from one registered annotation: the slides are the same
  propagated annotation, not independent replications. The layer bins come
  from a NeuN-trained classifier propagated to each stain by serial-section registration (QNP
  documentation, June 2026). These **classifier-derived layer-area fractions** may change because
  of anatomical remodeling, because an altered NeuN phenotype shifts where layer boundaries are
  drawn, or both. They are not evidence of layer thinning, neuronal loss or atrophy. They are a
  measurement caveat for MTG layer analyses and a hypothesis for later morphology work.

**Eligible regions.** Only **MTG and DFC** are cortical-layer-resolved in the June 2026 release.
Both have the same five bins (Layer1, Layer2, Layer3, Layer4, Layer5-6), and both have AT8
(`percent AT8 positive area`) and NeuN (`number of NeuN positive cells per area`) for all 84
donors in every layer, with no missing values.

- **Excluded, grey matter only:** AnG, FI, ITG, STG, V1C and ESOC.
- **Not cortical layers:** HIP (subfields) and MEC (transentorhinal left/right). They are never
  forced onto a layer axis; Section 7.8 audits them as their own internal anatomy.
- **Excluded, not cortex:** CaH.
- **Excluded, deprecated:** the deprecated Gabitto MTG tab, which duplicates the MTG layers.

The "multiregional" laminar analysis is therefore a **two-region** analysis. Its FDR families are
correspondingly small: 2 regions for each tissue test, and 2 × 6 = 12 region × cognition cells.

### 7.2 Regional burden versus laminar profile

For donor *i*, region *r* and layer *l*, with `y = log2(AT8 % area + 0.001)` (notebook 05's log
offset):

| Quantity | Definition | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Regional burden *B*ᵢᵣ | `log2` of the released **grey-matter** AT8 for that region | the region's total burden |
| Layer enrichment *D*ᵢᵣₗ | *y*ᵢᵣₗ − *B*ᵢᵣ | how much AT8 layer *l* carries relative to the region as a whole (log2 fold) |
| Relative laminar profile *P*ᵢᵣₗ | *D*ᵢᵣₗ minus its cohort mean for that layer | the donor's departure from the typical laminar distribution (Figure 4A) |
| Model profile | within-donor centring of *y* (donor fixed effects), layers in sum-to-zero contrasts; for cognition, the centred log-ratio of L1–L4 (*K* − 1 = 4 contrasts) | the inferential target, always as a 4-df block |
| Equal-layer cumulative curve *C*ᵢᵣₖ | share *s*ᵢᵣₗ = AT8ᵢᵣₗ / Σₗ AT8ᵢᵣₗ, summed from deep to superficial: L5–6, +L4, +L3, +L2, +L1 (= 1) | the **cumulative normalized layer-mean AT8 signal**: an equal-layer concentration profile (Figure 4B) |
| Area-weighted cumulative curve *C*ᴬ (MTG only) | the same with *s* ∝ released layer area × AT8 | the **area-weighted section contribution**: the share of the section's AT8-positive area in each layer bin |

**Why the burden term is a compatible whole-region measure but not an independent one.** Grey
matter is reproduced by a weighted sum of the five layers whose weights sum to 1 (R² ≥
`r sprintf("%.3f", min(lam_gm_check$r2))`), and it always lies inside the layer range; in MTG the
released layer areas reproduce it exactly. It is the area-weighted aggregate of the same
measurements. *B* is therefore the regional total, and *D* is a compositional decomposition of
it, not an independent second observation of burden. The regional summary captures the dominant
**scale component** of the layer measurements, while a smaller **relative-depth component**
remains. That split is a property of how five correlated, aggregated measurements decompose; it is
not an independent biological variance decomposition.

**The cumulative depth curve, and what it is not.** *C* is built from layer *means* (% area within
each bin) with every layer weighted equally, because DFC has no released layer areas and weights
must not be reverse-engineered from the AT8 values. It is a descriptive, scale-free summary of
how the relative AT8 signal accumulates across the five bins in anatomical order. It is **not** a
fraction of total cortical tau, a cumulative tau mass, a cortical-column distribution or evidence
of local propagation.

**Two estimands, not a primary and a check.** The equal-layer and area-weighted curves answer
different questions:

- **Equal-layer concentration profile** (*C*, both regions): how does marker concentration or
  density vary across the named cortical layers, giving each layer equal representational weight?
- **Area-weighted section contribution** (*C*ᴬ, MTG only): how much does each layer contribute to
  the section-level marker amount once the classifier-assigned layer area is incorporated?

They can legitimately disagree. When layer-area fractions themselves change with progression
(Section 7.1), the section contribution moves even if concentrations do not, and vice versa.
Neither is "correct"; a disagreement says that changing layer geometry matters for that marker.

**Representation sensitivity.** *P* divides each layer by a regional value built from those same
layers. The alternative is the centred log-ratio (clr), or equivalently an orthogonal pivot
log-contrast (ilr) basis, which uses no external denominator. Any donor-level log denominator
(grey matter, geometric mean) is a constant within donor, so the layer × progression *omnibus*
is invariant to it by construction. The representations differ in their per-layer slopes, and the
linear-scale cumulative curve *C* is a genuinely different representation with its own test.

**Choices that follow from this:**

- **Layer baselines** are removed before profiles are compared, by subtracting the cohort mean of
  each layer's *D* in Figure 4A and by layer main effects in every model.
- **No profile is ever re-weighted or optimized** against an outcome.
- **No layer is imputed.** None is missing.
- **NeuN (Section 7.5) uses notebook 05's tissue-association scale:** within-region × layer normal
  scores, which bound the two NeuN-floor donors. Its donor-region level is the donor mean, and
  its laminar profile is the deviation from that mean.

### 7.3 Analysis A — how much does the regional value discard?

```{r}
#| label: laminar-variance

lam_vc <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  d <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% mutate(lyr = layer)
  variance_components(d, "y", roi = "lyr") %>% mutate(region = r)
})
lam_prof <- lay %>% group_by(brain_region, layer) %>%
  summarise(sd_P = sd(P), mad_fold = 2^median(abs(P)), .groups = "drop")
lam_tert <- lay %>% group_by(brain_region, gp_tertile, layer) %>% summarise(s = sd(P), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(brain_region, gp_tertile) %>% summarise(sd_P = sqrt(mean(s^2)), .groups = "drop")
lam_gp_r2 <- map_dbl(set_names(LAM_REGIONS), function(r) {
  w <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% select(donor_id, layer, clr, gz) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = clr)
  Y <- scale(as.matrix(w[LAM_LAYERS]), scale = FALSE)
  1 - sum(residuals(lm(Y ~ w$gz))^2) / sum(Y^2)
})
# Do a donor's MTG and DFC profiles agree? Raw clr profiles, and profiles after removing the
# layer x progression trend (which both regions share). A donor-label permutation gives the
# null for the mean Spearman rho across layers.
lam_conc_tbl <- function(adjust) lay %>% group_by(brain_region, layer) %>%
  mutate(r = if (adjust) residuals(lm(clr ~ gz)) else clr - mean(clr)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(donor_id, brain_region, layer, r) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = brain_region, values_from = r) %>%
  arrange(layer, donor_id)
n_lam_donors <- n_distinct(lay$donor_id)
lam_conc <- map_dfr(c(Raw = FALSE, `Progression-adjusted` = TRUE), function(adj) {
  rr <- lam_conc_tbl(adj)
  stat <- function(perm) map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, function(l) { x <- rr[rr$layer == l, ]
    cor(x$MTG, x$DFC[perm], method = "spearman") })
  obs <- stat(seq_len(n_lam_donors))
  set.seed(BOOT_SEED)
  null <- replicate(B_BOOT, mean(stat(sample(n_lam_donors))))
  tibble(layer = LAM_LAYERS, rho = obs, mean_rho = mean(obs),
         p = (1 + sum(null >= mean(obs))) / (1 + B_BOOT),
         null_lo = quantile(null, 0.025), null_hi = quantile(null, 0.975))
}, .id = "version")
lam_conc_layer <- lam_conc %>% filter(version == "Progression-adjusted")
lam_conc_obs <- lam_conc_layer$mean_rho[1]; lam_conc_p <- lam_conc_layer$p[1]
lcr <- function(v, col) lam_conc[[col]][lam_conc$version == v][1]

lam_var_tbl <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  v <- lam_vc %>% filter(region == r); pr <- lam_prof %>% filter(brain_region == r)
  tt <- lam_tert %>% filter(brain_region == r)
  tibble(Region = r, Donors = n_distinct(lay$donor_id[lay$brain_region == r]),
         `Burden SD (log2)` = sd(lam_gm$burden[lam_gm$brain_region == r]),
         `Donor (burden) share` = v$share[v$component == "donor"],
         `Layer-baseline share` = v$share[v$component == "ROI"],
         `Donor × layer (profile + error) share` = v$share[v$component == "donor x ROI"],
         `Profile SD by layer (log2), L1 / L2 / L3 / L4 / L5–6` = paste(sprintf("%.2f", pr$sd_P), collapse = " / "),
         `Median |profile| as fold` = sprintf("%.2f×", median(pr$mad_fold)),
         `Profile SD within Global pTau tertile, low / mid / high` = paste(sprintf("%.2f", tt$sd_P), collapse = " / "),
         `Profile variance explained by Global pTau` = lam_gp_r2[[r]])
})
show_table(lam_var_tbl, caption = "Analysis A. Variance of log2 layer AT8 split into donor (regional burden), layer baseline, and donor × layer (laminar profile plus measurement error, which this design cannot separate), as in Figure 1D. Profile SD = SD over donors of the relative profile P. Tertiles are notebook 05's all-donor Global pTau tertiles.")
write_csv(lam_var_tbl, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_A_variance.csv"))
lv <- function(r, col) lam_var_tbl[[col]][lam_var_tbl$Region == r]
stopifnot("regional burden carries > 90% of layer AT8 variance in both regions" =
            all(lam_var_tbl$`Donor (burden) share` > 0.9))
```

```{r}
#| label: laminar-variance-numbers

lt3 <- function(r, t) lam_tert$sd_P[lam_tert$brain_region == r & lam_tert$gp_tertile == t]
conc_max <- lam_conc_layer %>% slice_max(rho, n = 2)
stopifnot("MTG and DFC residual profiles agree beyond donor-label permutation" = lam_conc_p < 0.05)
```

**Reading.**

- **The regional summary captures the dominant scale component.** The donor component of log layer
  AT8 is `r percent(lv("MTG", "Donor (burden) share"), 1)` (MTG) and
  `r percent(lv("DFC", "Donor (burden) share"), 1)` (DFC) of its variance. Layer baselines carry
  about 1%, and the donor × layer remainder (relative-depth profile plus measurement error) about
  3%. Because grey matter is an area-weighted aggregate of these same layers, this is a description
  of how five strongly correlated measurements decompose, not an estimate that a fixed fraction of
  tau biology is "regional".
- **The remaining profile is not negligible in tissue terms.** Relative to what the regional value
  and the typical laminar distribution imply, the median layer departs by
  `r lv("MTG", "Median |profile| as fold")` (MTG) and `r lv("DFC", "Median |profile| as fold")`
  (DFC). The profile SD reaches `r sprintf("%.2f", max(lam_prof$sd_P))` log2 units in L1, the most
  variable layer in both regions.
- **Donors at comparable progression differ.** Within each Global pTau tertile the profile SD is
  `r sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(lam_tert$sd_P), max(lam_tert$sd_P))` log2 units (Figure 4A).
- **Floor noise in MTG.** MTG's profile varies most in the lowest tertile (SD
  `r sprintf("%.2f", lt3("MTG", GT_LEVELS[1]))` vs `r sprintf("%.2f", lt3("MTG", GT_LEVELS[2]))`
  mid). There AT8 is near the stain floor, so part of that variation is sparse-signal noise, not
  organized pathology.
- **Progression organizes the profile in DFC, barely in MTG.** Global pTau explains
  `r percent(lam_gp_r2[["DFC"]], 1)` of the DFC profile variance but only
  `r percent(lam_gp_r2[["MTG"]], 1)` in MTG (Section 7.4).
- **Weak but detectable cross-region concordance** (Supplementary Figure S4B).
  Raw MTG and DFC profiles agree weakly (mean Spearman ρ across layers
  `r sprintf("%.2f", lcr("Raw", "mean_rho"))`, permutation p `r sprintf("%.3f", lcr("Raw", "p"))`).
  After the progression trend both regions share is removed, they still agree: mean ρ
  `r sprintf("%.2f", lam_conc_obs)`, permutation p `r sprintf("%.3f", lam_conc_p)`, strongest in
  `r paste(LAM_LAB[as.character(conc_max$layer)], collapse = " and ")` (ρ
  `r paste(sprintf("%.2f", conc_max$rho), collapse = " and ")`). Section-specific noise would not
  produce agreement between two regions sampled on different slides. Donor-level technical factors
  (fixation, staining batch) could. The concordance is weak; it does not establish a donor-wide
  laminar phenotype (no donor-level latent model is fitted), and the design cannot separate the
  remainder from region-specific variation and measurement error.

### 7.4 Analysis B — does the laminar profile change with progression?

**Model, per region.** `log2 AT8_layer ~ layer + layer × CPS_Global_pTau + donor`, with donor fixed
effects. The fixed effects absorb the regional burden and every other donor-level quantity, so
only the within-donor laminar profile informs the interaction. Layers are coded sum-to-zero.

**Target.** The 4-df **layer × progression block**, tested by a donor-cluster-robust Wald F (CR1;
F with 4 and *G* − 1 df). An exact multivariate profile test (Pillai, one row per donor) is given
as a cross-check. Layer-specific slopes (log2 relative AT8 per SD of Global pTau, summing to zero
across layers) are shown for display only, with donor-bootstrap intervals. BH FDR runs across the
eligible regions.

**Direct regional comparison.** Separate q-values cannot show that MTG and DFC differ. All 84
donors have both regions, so both are stacked in one model:
`log2 AT8 ~ region × layer + region × layer × CPS_Global_pTau + donor × region`, with a fixed
effect per donor-region (each region's own burden) and CR1 clustering on **donor**, so a donor's
two regions are not treated as independent. The target is the 4-df **region × layer × progression**
contrast, the difference between the two regions' layer × progression blocks. A paired
multivariate test (Pillai on the per-donor DFC − MTG clr difference) is the cross-check.

Global pTau enters every test continuously. Tertiles appear only in descriptive displays, and the
three reference values used to draw model curves (the tertile medians of `CPS_Global_pTau`) are
visualization anchors, not groups.

**Sensitivities.**

- the same block indexed by the region's own burden *B* instead of global progression;
- without the published severely affected donors;
- leave-one-donor-out stability of the omnibus p and of the L1 relative slope;
- representation: GM-relative *P* versus clr per-layer slopes, the ilr pivot basis, and the
  linear-scale cumulative curve *C* (its own 4-df test on the four non-terminal boundaries);
  in MTG, the area-weighted *C*ᴬ as a second estimand (section contribution), not as a check on
  the first;
- the region's absolute layer AT8 next to the relative profile (below), so a relative decrease is
  never read as an absolute one;
- conventional staging: the DFC layer profile against Braak stage instead of Global pTau.

```{r}
#| label: laminar-progression

# Donor-cluster-robust (CR1) Wald test of coefficients `idx` from an OLS fit on
# within-donor-demeaned data; the absorbed donor means are the fixed effects.
cr_wald <- function(X, y, cl, idx, R = NULL) {
  fit <- lm.fit(X, y); b <- fit$coefficients; e <- fit$residuals
  XtXi <- solve(crossprod(X)); G <- length(unique(cl)); N <- nrow(X); k <- ncol(X)
  meat <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(split(seq_len(N), cl), function(i) tcrossprod(crossprod(X[i, , drop = FALSE], e[i]))))
  V <- XtXi %*% meat %*% XtXi * (G / (G - 1)) * ((N - 1) / (N - k))
  if (is.null(R)) R <- diag(length(idx))
  bb <- R %*% b[idx]; VV <- R %*% V[idx, idx] %*% t(R)
  W <- drop(t(bb) %*% solve(VV, bb)); q <- nrow(R)
  list(b = b, V = V, F = W / q, df1 = q, df2 = G - 1, p = stats::pf(W / q, q, G - 1, lower.tail = FALSE))
}
demean_by <- function(M, g) M - apply(M, 2, function(v) ave(v, g))
LAM_CS <- contr.sum(length(LAM_LAYERS))
lam_omnibus_B <- function(d, expo) {
  L <- LAM_CS[as.integer(d$layer), ]
  X <- demean_by(cbind(L, L * d[[expo]]), d$donor_id)
  cr_wald(X, d$y - ave(d$y, d$donor_id), d$donor_id, 5:8)
}
lam_wide <- function(r, value = "clr") lay %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>%
  select(donor_id, layer, v = all_of(value), gz, burden, severe) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = v)
slopes_fun <- function(expo) function(w) {
  x <- zstd(w[[expo]]); setNames(map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, ~ unname(coef(lm(w[[.x]] ~ x))[2])), LAM_LAYERS)
}
lam_B <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  d <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% mutate(bz = zstd(burden))
  w <- lam_wide(r)
  og <- lam_omnibus_B(d, "gz"); ob <- lam_omnibus_B(d, "bz")
  pil <- anova(lm(as.matrix(w[LAM_LAYERS[1:4]]) ~ w$gz))
  bind_rows(
    cluster_bootstrap(w, slopes_fun("gz"), B_BOOT, seed = BOOT_SEED) %>% mutate(index = "Global pTau"),
    cluster_bootstrap(w, slopes_fun("burden"), B_BOOT, seed = BOOT_SEED) %>% mutate(index = "Regional burden")
  ) %>% mutate(region = r, n = nrow(w),
               F = if_else(index == "Global pTau", og$F, ob$F),
               p = if_else(index == "Global pTau", og$p, ob$p),
               pillai_p = if_else(index == "Global pTau", pil$`Pr(>F)`[2], NA_real_))
})
# BH over the region family (one omnibus per region and index)
lam_B_omni <- lam_B %>% distinct(index, region, n, F, p, pillai_p) %>%
  group_by(index) %>% mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH")) %>% ungroup()
lam_B <- lam_B %>% left_join(lam_B_omni %>% select(index, region, q), by = c("index", "region"))
stopifnot("every bootstrap resample fitted" = all(lam_B$n_boot_ok == B_BOOT),
          "layer-specific progression slopes sum to zero" =
            all(abs(tapply(lam_B$estimate, paste(lam_B$region, lam_B$index), sum)) < 1e-8))
lb <- function(r, col = "q", ix = "Global pTau") lam_B_omni[[col]][lam_B_omni$region == r & lam_B_omni$index == ix]
lbs <- function(r, l, ix = "Global pTau") { x <- lam_B %>% filter(region == r, term == l, index == ix); fmt_sci(x$estimate, x$lo, x$hi) }
stopifnot("DFC laminar AT8 profile changes with Global pTau (FDR < 0.05)" = lb("DFC") < 0.05,
          "MTG's layer x progression block is weaker but q < 0.05" = lb("MTG") < 0.05 && lb("MTG") > lb("DFC"),
          "the CR1 Wald and Pillai tests agree on DFC" = lb("DFC", "pillai_p") < 0.05)

lam_B_omni %>% transmute(Index = index, Region = region, Donors = n, `F (4, G−1)` = F,
                         p = format(p, digits = 2), `q (BH, regions)` = format(q, digits = 2),
                         `Pillai p (cross-check)` = if_else(is.na(pillai_p), "–", format(pillai_p, digits = 2))) %>%
  show_table(caption = "Analysis B omnibus: the 4-df layer × progression block per region (donor fixed effects; CR1 donor-cluster Wald). Primary index: CPS_Global_pTau. Sensitivity: the region's own AT8 burden.")
lam_B %>% mutate(cell = fmt_sci(estimate, lo, hi), Layer = LAM_LAB[term]) %>%
  select(Index = index, Region = region, Layer, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Layer, values_from = cell) %>%
  show_table(caption = sprintf("Layer-specific change of the relative laminar profile (log2 per SD of the index; sums to zero across layers), donor-bootstrap 95%% CI (%d resamples). Display quantities; not tested one by one.", B_BOOT))
write_csv(lam_B %>% left_join(lam_B_omni %>% select(index, region, pillai_p_omni = pillai_p), by = c("index", "region")),
          file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_B_progression.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: laminar-cumulative

# Cumulative normalized layer-mean AT8 signal, deep -> superficial. k = 1 is L5-6 alone,
# k = 5 is all five layers (= 1 by construction).
LAM_DEEP <- rev(LAM_LAYERS)
CUM_LAB <- c("L5–6", "+ L4", "+ L3", "+ L2", "+ L1")
cum_build <- function(d, weight = NULL) d %>%
  mutate(.w = if (is.null(weight)) 1 else .data[[weight]]) %>%
  group_by(brain_region, donor_id) %>%
  mutate(s = .w * at8 / sum(.w * at8)) %>%
  arrange(desc(as.integer(layer)), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(C = cumsum(s), k = row_number()) %>% ungroup() %>% select(-.w)
lam_cum <- cum_build(lay)
lam_cum_A <- cum_build(lay %>% filter(brain_region == "MTG") %>%
                         left_join(lam_area %>% select(donor_id, layer, area), by = c("donor_id", "layer")),
                       weight = "area")
stopifnot(
  "cumulative curves start at the deepest layer and run L5-6 -> L1" =
    all(lam_cum$layer[lam_cum$k == 1] == "Layer5-6") && all(lam_cum$layer[lam_cum$k == 5] == "Layer1"),
  "cumulative curves are non-decreasing and bounded in (0, 1]" =
    all(lam_cum$C > 0 & lam_cum$C <= 1 + 1e-12) &&
    all(lam_cum %>% group_by(brain_region, donor_id) %>% summarise(ok = all(diff(C) >= 0), .groups = "drop") %>% pull(ok)),
  "every cumulative curve terminates at exactly 1" =
    all(abs(lam_cum$C[lam_cum$k == 5] - 1) < 1e-12) && all(abs(lam_cum_A$C[lam_cum_A$k == 5] - 1) < 1e-12),
  "area-weighted MTG curve uses the released layer areas for every donor x layer" =
    nrow(lam_cum_A) == 420L && !anyNA(lam_cum_A$C)
)

# 4-df test of the cumulative curve against continuous Global pTau: the four non-terminal
# boundaries stacked per donor, CR1 donor-cluster Wald (Pillai as cross-check).
cum_test <- function(cd, value = "C") {
  z <- cd %>% filter(k < 5)
  Bk <- diag(4)[z$k, ]
  o <- cr_wald(cbind(Bk, Bk * z$gz), z[[value]], z$donor_id, 5:8)
  w <- z %>% select(donor_id, k, v = all_of(value), gz) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = v)
  Y <- as.matrix(w[as.character(1:4)])
  sl <- coef(lm(Y ~ zstd(w$gz)))[2, ]
  tibble(k = 1:4, slope = unname(sl), std = unname(sl / apply(Y, 2, sd)),
         n = nrow(w), F = o$F, df2 = o$df2, p = o$p,
         pillai_p = anova(lm(Y ~ w$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2])
}
lam_cum_test <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, ~ cum_test(lam_cum %>% filter(brain_region == .x)) %>%
            mutate(region = .x, representation = "Layer-mean (equal weight)")),
  cum_test(lam_cum_A) %>% mutate(region = "MTG", representation = "Area-weighted (MTG)"))

# Model-derived curves: clr ~ CPS_Global_pTau per region (equivalent to the donor fixed-effects
# layer x progression model), evaluated at the three anchors, closed back to shares and
# accumulated deep -> superficial. Donor-bootstrap percentile bands.
CUM_ANCHORS <- c(tapply(donor$CPS_Global_pTau, donor$gp_tertile, median))
cum_predict <- function(w) {
  f <- lm(as.matrix(w[LAM_LAYERS]) ~ w$CPS_Global_pTau)
  out <- map(seq_along(CUM_ANCHORS), function(j) {
    pr <- coef(f)[1, ] + coef(f)[2, ] * CUM_ANCHORS[[j]]
    s <- 2^pr / sum(2^pr)
    setNames(cumsum(s[LAM_DEEP]), paste0(j, "_", 1:5))
  })
  unlist(out)
}
lam_cum_model <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  w <- lam_wide(r) %>% left_join(donor %>% select(donor_id, CPS_Global_pTau), by = "donor_id")
  cluster_bootstrap(w, cum_predict, B_BOOT, seed = BOOT_SEED) %>% mutate(region = r)
}) %>% separate(term, c("anchor", "k"), sep = "_", convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(anchor = GT_LEVELS[anchor], anchor_value = unname(CUM_ANCHORS[anchor]))
stopifnot(
  "model-derived cumulative curves terminate at 1 and stay bounded" =
    all(abs(lam_cum_model$estimate[lam_cum_model$k == 5] - 1) < 1e-12) &&
    all(lam_cum_model$estimate > 0 & lam_cum_model$estimate <= 1 + 1e-12),
  "every bootstrap resample fitted" = all(lam_cum_model$n_boot_ok == B_BOOT),
  "anchors are ordered low < mid < high Global pTau" = !is.unsorted(CUM_ANCHORS, strictly = TRUE)
)
lcm <- function(r, a, k) lam_cum_model %>% filter(region == r, anchor == GT_LEVELS[a], k == !!k)
lcm_fmt <- function(r, a, k) { x <- lcm(r, a, k); fmt_ci(x$estimate, x$lo, x$hi) }
lct <- function(r, col = "p", rep = "Layer-mean (equal weight)") lam_cum_test[[col]][lam_cum_test$region == r & lam_cum_test$representation == rep][1]
write_csv(lam_cum %>% select(brain_region, donor_id, layer, k, s, C, CPS_Global_pTau, gp_tertile, severe),
          file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_cumulative_donor.csv"))
write_csv(lam_cum_model, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_cumulative_model.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: laminar-progression-direct

# Direct comparison: both regions stacked, a fixed effect per donor x region, CR1 clustered
# on donor; contrast = DFC block - MTG block of the layer x progression interaction.
lam_direct <- function(d) {
  d <- d %>% mutate(cell = paste(donor_id, brain_region), isD = as.numeric(brain_region == "DFC"))
  L <- LAM_CS[as.integer(d$layer), ]
  X <- demean_by(cbind(L * (1 - d$isD), L * d$isD, L * d$gz * (1 - d$isD), L * d$gz * d$isD), d$cell)
  y <- d$y - ave(d$y, d$cell)
  o <- cr_wald(X, y, d$donor_id, 1:16, R = cbind(matrix(0, 4, 8), -diag(4), diag(4)))
  wm <- d %>% filter(brain_region == "MTG") %>% select(donor_id, layer, clr, gz) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = clr)
  wd <- d %>% filter(brain_region == "DFC") %>% select(donor_id, layer, clr) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = clr)
  stopifnot("paired MTG/DFC rows align by donor" = identical(wm$donor_id, wd$donor_id))
  dif <- as.matrix(wd[LAM_LAYERS[1:4]]) - as.matrix(wm[LAM_LAYERS[1:4]])
  tibble(n = n_distinct(d$donor_id), F = o$F, df1 = o$df1, df2 = o$df2, p = o$p,
         pillai_p = anova(lm(dif ~ wm$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2])
}
stopifnot("every donor has both MTG and DFC layer profiles" =
            all(count(distinct(lay, donor_id, brain_region), donor_id)$n == 2))
lam_dir <- bind_rows(lam_direct(lay) %>% mutate(set = "All donors"),
                     lam_direct(lay %>% filter(!severe)) %>% mutate(set = "Without severely affected donors"))

# Robustness of each region's progression-depth result.
ilr_basis <- function(K) {          # pivot coordinates: layer j versus all deeper layers
  V <- matrix(0, K, K - 1)
  for (j in seq_len(K - 1)) { r <- K - j; V[j, j] <- sqrt(r / (r + 1)); V[(j + 1):K, j] <- -sqrt(1 / (r * (r + 1))) }
  V
}
LAM_ILR <- ilr_basis(5)
stopifnot("ilr basis is orthonormal and orthogonal to the constant" =
            max(abs(crossprod(LAM_ILR) - diag(4))) < 1e-12 && max(abs(colSums(LAM_ILR))) < 1e-12)
ilr_test <- function(r) {
  w <- lam_wide(r); Z <- as.matrix(w[LAM_LAYERS]) %*% LAM_ILR
  z <- tibble(donor_id = rep(w$donor_id, 4), gz = rep(w$gz, 4), k = rep(1:4, each = nrow(w)), v = c(Z))
  Bk <- diag(4)[z$k, ]
  cr_wald(cbind(Bk, Bk * z$gz), z$v, z$donor_id, 5:8)
}
lam_loo <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  d <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r); w <- lam_wide(r)
  map_dfr(unique(d$donor_id), function(i) {
    wi <- w %>% filter(donor_id != i)
    tibble(region = r, left_out = i, p = lam_omnibus_B(d %>% filter(donor_id != i), "gz")$p,
           l1 = unname(coef(lm(wi$Layer1 ~ zstd(wi$gz)))[2]))
  })
})
lam_robust <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  d <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r); lo <- lam_loo %>% filter(region == r); il <- ilr_test(r)
  tibble(region = r,
         p_primary = lb(r, "p"),
         p_no_sa = lam_omnibus_B(d %>% filter(!severe), "gz")$p, n_no_sa = n_distinct(d$donor_id[!d$severe]),
         loo_p_max = max(lo$p), loo_worst = lo$left_out[which.max(lo$p)],
         loo_l1_lo = min(lo$l1), loo_l1_hi = max(lo$l1),
         ilr_F = il$F, ilr_p = il$p, fe_F = lb(r, "F"),
         cum_p = lct(r), cum_A_p = if (r == "MTG") lct("MTG", "p", "Area-weighted (MTG)") else NA_real_)
})
# Per-layer slopes of the GM-relative profile (primary display scale) next to the clr slopes.
lam_rep_slopes <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  wD <- lam_wide(r, "D"); wc <- lam_wide(r, "clr")
  bind_rows(tibble(layer = LAM_LAYERS, slope = slopes_fun("gz")(wD), representation = "GM-relative (P)"),
            tibble(layer = LAM_LAYERS, slope = slopes_fun("gz")(wc), representation = "Centred log-ratio")) %>%
    mutate(region = r)
})
lr <- function(r, col) lam_robust[[col]][lam_robust$region == r]
ldir <- function(col, s = "All donors") lam_dir[[col]][lam_dir$set == s]
stopifnot(
  "MTG and DFC differ in how relative layer AT8 changes with Global pTau (direct test)" = ldir("p") < 0.05,
  "the direct region difference holds without the severely affected donors" =
    ldir("p", "Without severely affected donors") < 0.05 && ldir("pillai_p") < 0.05,
  "DFC progression-depth result survives SA exclusion, every leave-one-out and the cumulative representation" =
    lr("DFC", "p_no_sa") < 0.05 && lr("DFC", "loo_p_max") < 0.05 && lr("DFC", "cum_p") < 0.05 &&
    lr("DFC", "loo_l1_hi") < 0,
  "the log-contrast omnibus is basis-invariant up to the CR1 small-sample factor" =
    all(abs(lam_robust$ilr_F / lam_robust$fe_F - 1) < 0.02),
  "GM-relative and clr slopes differ only by a constant within region" =
    lam_rep_slopes %>% pivot_wider(names_from = representation, values_from = slope) %>%
      group_by(region) %>% summarise(s = sd(`GM-relative (P)` - `Centred log-ratio`), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pull(s) %>% max() < 1e-10
)

bind_rows(
  lam_B_omni %>% filter(index == "Global pTau") %>%
    transmute(Test = paste(region, "layer × Global pTau"), Donors = n, F = sprintf("%.2f (4, %d)", F, n - 1L),
              p = format(p, digits = 2), `Cross-check p (Pillai)` = format(pillai_p, digits = 2)),
  lam_dir %>% transmute(Test = paste0("Region × layer × Global pTau (DFC vs MTG)", if_else(set == "All donors", "", ", without SA donors")),
                        Donors = n, F = sprintf("%.2f (%d, %d)", F, df1, df2),
                        p = format(p, digits = 2), `Cross-check p (Pillai)` = format(pillai_p, digits = 2))
) %>% show_table(caption = "Progression-depth omnibus tests. Per-region rows: donor fixed effects, CR1 donor-cluster Wald (as in the table above). Direct row: MTG and DFC stacked with a fixed effect per donor × region, CR1 clustered on donor; cross-check = Pillai test of the per-donor DFC − MTG clr difference on Global pTau.")
lam_robust %>% transmute(Region = region,
                         `Primary p` = format(p_primary, digits = 2),
                         `Without SA donors p` = sprintf("%s (n = %d)", format(p_no_sa, digits = 2), n_no_sa),
                         `Leave-one-out: largest p` = sprintf("%s (without %s)", format(loo_p_max, digits = 2), loo_worst),
                         `Leave-one-out: L1 slope range` = sprintf("%+.2f to %+.2f", loo_l1_lo, loo_l1_hi),
                         `ilr pivot basis p` = format(ilr_p, digits = 2),
                         `Cumulative curve C p` = format(cum_p, digits = 2),
                         `Area-weighted Cᴬ p` = if_else(is.na(cum_A_p), "no areas released", format(cum_A_p, digits = 2))) %>%
  show_table(caption = "Robustness of the layer × Global pTau result. L1 slope = clr log2 relative AT8 per SD of Global pTau. The ilr test reuses the same log-ratio information in an orthonormal pivot basis; the cumulative-curve tests use the linear-scale shares and are a genuinely different representation.")
write_csv(lam_dir, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_B_direct_region_test.csv"))
write_csv(lam_robust, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_B_robustness.csv"))
write_csv(lam_cum_test, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_B_cumulative_tests.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: laminar-absolute-relative

# Absolute: log2 layer AT8 on Global pTau, one regression per layer, donor = unit.
# Relative: the Figure 4A profile P (layer relative to grey matter, centred by layer).
# Standardized slope = Pearson r with Global pTau (SD of the layer quantity per SD); the raw
# slope (log2 per SD of Global pTau) is kept alongside. Both use the identical donor x layer rows.
ABSREL <- c(abs = "Absolute", rel = "Relative")
absrel_wide <- function(r) lay %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% select(donor_id, layer, abs = y, rel = P, gz) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = c(abs, rel))
absrel_stat <- function(w) unlist(map(names(ABSREL), function(k)
  setNames(map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, ~ cor(w[[paste0(k, "_", .x)]], w$gz)), paste0(k, "_", LAM_LAYERS))))
lam_absrel <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  w <- absrel_wide(r)
  stopifnot("absolute and relative AT8 share the same 84 donors x 5 layers, with no missing value" =
              nrow(w) == 84L && !anyNA(w) && setequal(names(w), c("donor_id", "gz", paste0(rep(names(ABSREL), each = 5), "_", LAM_LAYERS))))
  raw <- unlist(map(names(ABSREL), function(k)
    setNames(map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, ~ unname(coef(lm(w[[paste0(k, "_", .x)]] ~ w$gz))[2])), paste0(k, "_", LAM_LAYERS))))
  cluster_bootstrap(w, absrel_stat, B_BOOT, seed = BOOT_SEED) %>%
    mutate(raw = unname(raw[term]), region = r, n = nrow(w),
           p_abs = anova(lm(as.matrix(w[paste0("abs_", LAM_LAYERS)]) ~ w$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2])
}) %>% separate(term, c("rep", "layer"), sep = "_", extra = "merge") %>%
  mutate(representation = unname(ABSREL[rep]), region = factor(region, levels = LAM_REGIONS))
lar <- function(r, l, k = "Absolute", col = "raw") lam_absrel[[col]][lam_absrel$region == r & lam_absrel$layer == l & lam_absrel$representation == k]
lar_fmt <- function(r, l, k = "Absolute") sprintf("%+.2f", lar(r, l, k))
stopifnot(
  "every bootstrap resample fitted" = all(lam_absrel$n_boot_ok == B_BOOT),
  "relative raw slopes equal the GM-relative slopes of the representation check" =
    max(abs(lam_absrel %>% filter(representation == "Relative") %>% arrange(region, layer) %>% pull(raw) -
              lam_rep_slopes %>% filter(representation == "GM-relative (P)") %>%
                mutate(region = factor(region, levels = LAM_REGIONS)) %>% arrange(region, layer) %>% pull(slope))) < 1e-10,
  "absolute AT8 rises with Global pTau in every layer of both regions (as stated)" =
    all(lam_absrel$raw[lam_absrel$representation == "Absolute"] > 0) &&
    all(lam_absrel$lo[lam_absrel$representation == "Absolute"] > 0),
  "DFC: L1 has the smallest absolute rise and a relative decrease; L4 the largest absolute rise (as stated)" =
    lar("DFC", "Layer1") == min(lam_absrel$raw[lam_absrel$region == "DFC" & lam_absrel$representation == "Absolute"]) &&
    lar("DFC", "Layer4") == max(lam_absrel$raw[lam_absrel$region == "DFC" & lam_absrel$representation == "Absolute"]) &&
    lar("DFC", "Layer1", "Relative") < 0
)
lam_absrel %>% mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f (%s)", raw, fmt_ci(estimate, lo, hi)), Layer = LAM_LAB[layer]) %>%
  select(Region = region, Representation = representation, Layer, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Layer, values_from = cell) %>%
  show_table(caption = sprintf("Absolute versus relative layer AT8 against continuous Global pTau. Cell = raw slope (log2 per SD of Global pTau) and, in brackets, the standardized slope (Pearson r) with its donor-bootstrap 95%% CI (%d resamples). Absolute = log2 layer AT8; relative = the Figure 4A profile P. Joint test that all five absolute slopes are zero (Pillai): MTG p = %s, DFC p = %s; the relative omnibus is the layer × Global pTau test above.",
                               B_BOOT, format(lam_absrel$p_abs[lam_absrel$region == "MTG"][1], digits = 2), format(lam_absrel$p_abs[lam_absrel$region == "DFC"][1], digits = 2)))
write_csv(lam_absrel, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_B_absolute_vs_relative.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: laminar-braak

# Conventional-staging sensitivity for DFC only: the same donor fixed-effects layer x stage
# model with Braak stage (0-VI) as an ordered score; Notebook 05's Braak groups as a check.
braak_tbl <- donor %>% transmute(donor_id, braak_num = as.integer(braak_stage) - 1L, braak_group)
d_bk <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == "DFC") %>% left_join(braak_tbl, by = "donor_id")
bk_don <- distinct(d_bk, donor_id, braak_num)
d_bk <- d_bk %>% mutate(bkz = (braak_num - mean(bk_don$braak_num)) / sd(bk_don$braak_num))
lam_braak_lin <- lam_omnibus_B(d_bk, "bkz")
G_bk <- model.matrix(~ braak_group, d_bk)[, -1]
L_bk <- LAM_CS[as.integer(d_bk$layer), ]
lam_braak_cat <- cr_wald(demean_by(cbind(L_bk, L_bk * G_bk[, 1], L_bk * G_bk[, 2], L_bk * G_bk[, 3]), d_bk$donor_id),
                         d_bk$y - ave(d_bk$y, d_bk$donor_id), d_bk$donor_id, 5:16)
w_bk <- lam_wide("DFC", "P") %>% left_join(braak_tbl, by = "donor_id")
lam_braak_slopes <- setNames(map_dbl(LAM_LAYERS, ~ unname(coef(lm(w_bk[[.x]] ~ zstd(w_bk$braak_num)))[2])), LAM_LAYERS)
lam_braak_means <- d_bk %>% group_by(braak_group, layer) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(P), n = n_distinct(donor_id), .groups = "drop")
gp_dfc_slopes <- setNames(lam_rep_slopes$slope[lam_rep_slopes$region == "DFC" & lam_rep_slopes$representation == "GM-relative (P)"], LAM_LAYERS)
stopifnot(
  "Braak stage is complete for all 84 donors" = !anyNA(bk_don$braak_num) && nrow(bk_don) == 84L,
  "DFC layer profile changes with Braak stage, in the Global pTau direction for L1, L4 and L5-6 (as stated)" =
    lam_braak_lin$p < 0.05 && all(sign(lam_braak_slopes[c(1, 4, 5)]) == sign(gp_dfc_slopes[c(1, 4, 5)]))
)
tibble(`Stage index` = c("Braak stage, ordered score (0–VI)", "Braak group (0–III, IV, V, VI), categorical"),
       F = c(sprintf("%.2f (4, %d)", lam_braak_lin$F, lam_braak_lin$df2), sprintf("%.2f (12, %d)", lam_braak_cat$F, lam_braak_cat$df2)),
       p = format(c(lam_braak_lin$p, lam_braak_cat$p), digits = 2),
       `Relative slope per SD, L1 / L2 / L3 / L4 / L5–6` = c(paste(sprintf("%+.2f", lam_braak_slopes), collapse = " / "), "–"),
       `Global pTau slope, same layers` = c(paste(sprintf("%+.2f", gp_dfc_slopes), collapse = " / "), "–")) %>%
  show_table(caption = "DFC conventional-staging sensitivity: the layer × stage block (donor fixed effects, CR1 donor-cluster Wald) with Braak stage in place of CPS_Global_pTau. Slopes are the GM-relative profile per SD of the stage score. Not refitted for any other marker or region.")
write_csv(lam_braak_means, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_B_DFC_braak_profile.csv"))
```

**Reading.**

- **DFC: a clear progression-associated redistribution** (layer × Global pTau F
  `r sprintf("%.1f", lb("DFC", "F"))`, q `r format(lb("DFC"), digits = 2)`; Pillai p
  `r format(lb("DFC", "pillai_p"), digits = 2)`). At higher Global pTau, L1 carries a smaller
  relative share of the region's AT8 (`r lbs("DFC", "Layer1")` log2 per SD) and L4
  (`r lbs("DFC", "Layer4")`) and L5–6 (`r lbs("DFC", "Layer5-6")`) a larger one. On the cumulative
  curve (Figure 4B), the deep three bins (L5–6 to L3) carry
  `r lcm_fmt("DFC", 1, 3)` of the normalized layer-mean signal at the low anchor and
  `r lcm_fmt("DFC", 3, 3)` at the high anchor.
- **Relative depletion is not absolute decline.** Absolute AT8 rises with Global pTau in every
  layer of both regions (Supplementary Figure S4A). In DFC the absolute rise is smallest in L1
  (`r lar_fmt("DFC", "Layer1")` log2 per SD) and largest in L4 (`r lar_fmt("DFC", "Layer4")`);
  L1's relative share falls only because the other layers rise faster. So: **AT8 increases with
  disease progression in every DFC layer, but its increase is disproportionately greater in deeper
  cortical compartments, producing a reproducible change in relative cortical-depth organization.**
- **MTG: same direction, much weaker** (q `r format(lb("MTG"), digits = 2)`; L1
  `r lbs("MTG", "Layer1")`; deep three bins `r lcm_fmt("MTG", 1, 3)` low vs
  `r lcm_fmt("MTG", 3, 3)` high).
- **The regions differ directly.** The region × layer × Global pTau contrast is supported
  (F `r sprintf("%.1f", ldir("F"))` on (`r ldir("df1")`, `r ldir("df2")`) df, p
  `r format(ldir("p"), digits = 2)`; paired Pillai p `r format(ldir("pillai_p"), digits = 2)`;
  without the severely affected donors p
  `r format(ldir("p", "Without severely affected donors"), digits = 2)`). DFC's depth profile
  changes more with progression than MTG's. This, not the two separate q-values, is the basis for
  calling the effect stronger in DFC.
- **Robust in DFC.** Without the severely affected donors p
  `r format(lr("DFC", "p_no_sa"), digits = 2)`; the largest leave-one-out p is
  `r format(lr("DFC", "loo_p_max"), digits = 2)` and the L1 slope stays between
  `r sprintf("%+.2f and %+.2f", lr("DFC", "loo_l1_lo"), lr("DFC", "loo_l1_hi"))`; the linear-scale
  cumulative curve gives p `r format(lr("DFC", "cum_p"), digits = 2)`.
- **Braak-stage sensitivity converges in DFC.** With Braak stage in place of Global pTau, the DFC
  layer × stage block is supported (ordered score p `r format(lam_braak_lin$p, digits = 2)`;
  Braak groups p `r format(lam_braak_cat$p, digits = 2)`), with the same directions: L1
  `r sprintf("%+.2f", lam_braak_slopes[["Layer1"]])`, L4 `r sprintf("%+.2f", lam_braak_slopes[["Layer4"]])`,
  L5–6 `r sprintf("%+.2f", lam_braak_slopes[["Layer5-6"]])` per SD of stage (Supplementary Figure
  S5B). This is a convergent conventional-stage sensitivity, not independent validation: Braak
  stage is another tau-based staging system, read from the same pathology.
- **Fragile in MTG.** Without the severely affected donors p
  `r format(lr("MTG", "p_no_sa"), digits = 2)`, but single donors move it to
  `r format(lr("MTG", "loo_p_max"), digits = 2)`; the equal-layer cumulative curve gives
  `r format(lr("MTG", "cum_p"), digits = 2)`. MTG's equal-layer change is at the edge of detection.
- **MTG section contribution is a different quantity.** The area-weighted curve (share of the
  section's AT8-positive area per layer bin) moves in the same direction but is not supported
  (p `r format(lr("MTG", "cum_A_p"), digits = 2)`). This does not invalidate the equal-layer
  estimate: MTG's classifier-derived layer-area fractions themselves change with progression
  (Section 7.1), and that changing geometry contributes to the difference between the two.
- **Representation.** The log-contrast omnibus does not depend on whether layers are expressed
  relative to grey matter, to their geometric mean (clr) or in an ilr pivot basis (F
  `r sprintf("%.2f", lr("DFC", "fe_F"))` vs `r sprintf("%.2f", lr("DFC", "ilr_F"))` in DFC). The
  GM-relative and clr per-layer slopes differ only by a common constant (Supplementary Figure S4C).
  The depth pattern stays recognizable under every representation.
- **Global versus local cannot be separated.** Indexed by the region's own AT8 burden, the same
  pattern is as strong or stronger (q `r format(lb("DFC", "q", "Regional burden"), digits = 2)`
  DFC, `r format(lb("MTG", "q", "Regional burden"), digits = 2)` MTG). Global stage and local
  accumulation are collinear here.
- **What this is and is not.** This is a progression-associated redistribution in a
  cross-sectional, aggregate layer summary: donors at higher Global pTau have a relatively
  deeper-weighted AT8 profile. It is consistent with the classical concentration of
  neurofibrillary pathology in pyramidal-neuron-rich layers at advanced stages, and some of the
  low-stage L1 weighting may be near-floor or neuropil-thread signal. It does not show tau moving
  or spreading between layers, and it says nothing about the order in which layers accumulate
  pathology within a donor.

### 7.5 Analysis C — AT8–NeuN laminar covariation

**Model, per region** (both stains as within-region × layer normal scores, donor fixed effects):

`NeuN_l ~ layer + layer × regional AT8 burden + layer × AT8 laminar deviation_l + donor`

- **AT8 laminar deviation:** the layer's AT8 normal score minus the donor's mean over layers.
- **Regional burden:** the grey-matter AT8 normal score.

Each term has a distinct reading:

- **Donor effect:** absorbs the donor-region NeuN level and the regional AT8 burden.
- **Layer × burden (4 df):** whether the NeuN laminar profile shifts with regional tau burden.
- **Layer-specific deviation slopes (5):** the **within-donor, at-comparable-burden** AT8 → NeuN
  association in each layer.

**Primary target.** Equality of the five deviation slopes (4-df heterogeneity test, CR1 Wald), with
BH across regions. This is the Mundlak form of `NeuN ~ AT8 × layer + donor`. The plain
fixed-effects version would force the burden-related laminar shift to equal the within-donor
slope.

**Severe-donor sensitivities** (normal scores kept from the full cohort, as in Section 3.3):

- **all donors;**
- **without the `r sum(donor$severe)` published severely affected donors:** the main sensitivity;
- **without the two NeuN-floor donors:** a diagnostic.

```{r}
#| label: laminar-neun

lam_fit_C <- function(d) {
  L <- LAM_CS[as.integer(d$layer), ]; Lf <- model.matrix(~ 0 + layer, d)
  X <- demean_by(cbind(L, L * d$at8_gm_ns, Lf * d$at8_w), d$donor_id)
  y <- d$neun_ns - ave(d$neun_ns, d$donor_id)
  het <- cr_wald(X, y, d$donor_id, 9:13, R = cbind(diag(4), -1))
  bur <- cr_wald(X, y, d$donor_id, 5:8)
  Xp <- demean_by(cbind(L, L * d$at8_gm_ns, d$at8_w), d$donor_id)
  pooled <- cr_wald(Xp, y, d$donor_id, 9)
  list(slopes = setNames(het$b[9:13], LAM_LAYERS), het_F = het$F, het_p = het$p,
       burden_p = bur$p, shift = c(bur$b[5:8], -sum(bur$b[5:8])), pooled = pooled$b[9], pooled_se = sqrt(pooled$V[9, 9]), df2 = het$df2)
}
LAM_C_VARIANTS <- list(`All donors` = character(0),
                       `Without severely affected donors` = severe_ids,
                       `Without the 2 NeuN-floor donors` = NEUN_FLOOR_DONORS)
lam_C <- imap_dfr(LAM_C_VARIANTS, function(drop, nm) map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  d <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r, !donor_id %in% drop)
  o <- lam_fit_C(d)
  cluster_bootstrap(d, function(x) lam_fit_C(x)$slopes, B_BOOT, seed = BOOT_SEED) %>%
    mutate(region = r, variant = nm, n = n_distinct(d$donor_id), het_F = o$het_F, het_p = o$het_p,
           burden_p = o$burden_p, pooled = o$pooled,
           shift = paste(sprintf("%+.2f", o$shift), collapse = " / "),
           pooled_lo = o$pooled - qt(0.975, o$df2) * o$pooled_se, pooled_hi = o$pooled + qt(0.975, o$df2) * o$pooled_se)
}))
stopifnot("every bootstrap resample fitted" = all(lam_C$n_boot_ok == B_BOOT))
lam_C_omni <- lam_C %>% distinct(variant, region, n, het_F, het_p, burden_p, shift, pooled, pooled_lo, pooled_hi) %>%
  group_by(variant) %>% mutate(het_q = p.adjust(het_p, "BH"), burden_q = p.adjust(burden_p, "BH")) %>% ungroup()
# A cell's reading "changes materially" without the severely affected donors if its sign
# flips with |slope| >= 0.1 on both sides, or it moves by >= 0.2 SD. Display rule only.
lam_C_flag <- lam_C %>% filter(variant %in% names(LAM_C_VARIANTS)[1:2]) %>%
  mutate(v = if_else(variant == "All donors", "all", "nosa")) %>%
  select(region, term, v, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = v, values_from = estimate, names_prefix = "estimate_") %>%
  mutate(changes = (sign(estimate_all) != sign(estimate_nosa) & pmin(abs(estimate_all), abs(estimate_nosa)) >= 0.1) |
           abs(estimate_all - estimate_nosa) >= 0.2)
lc <- function(r, col = "het_q", v = "All donors") lam_C_omni[[col]][lam_C_omni$region == r & lam_C_omni$variant == v]
lcs <- function(r, l, v = "All donors") { x <- lam_C %>% filter(region == r, term == l, variant == v); fmt_sci(x$estimate, x$lo, x$hi) }
lcp <- function(r, v = "All donors") { x <- lam_C_omni %>% filter(region == r, variant == v); fmt_sci(x$pooled, x$pooled_lo, x$pooled_hi) }
stopifnot(
  "MTG layer heterogeneity survives FDR in every donor set" =
    all(lam_C_omni$het_q[lam_C_omni$region == "MTG"] < 0.05),
  "DFC layer heterogeneity is not supported with or without severely affected donors" =
    all(lam_C_omni$het_q[lam_C_omni$region == "DFC"] >= 0.05),
  "only L1 changes materially without the severely affected donors" =
    all(lam_C_flag$term[lam_C_flag$changes] == "Layer1"),
  "MTG NeuN profile shift survives SA exclusion; DFC's does not, but survives the floor-only drop" =
    lc("MTG", "burden_q", "Without severely affected donors") < 0.05 && lc("DFC", "burden_q") < 0.05 &&
    lc("DFC", "burden_q", "Without severely affected donors") >= 0.05 &&
    lc("DFC", "burden_q", "Without the 2 NeuN-floor donors") < 0.05
)

lam_C_omni %>% transmute(Variant = variant, Region = region, Donors = n,
                         `Pooled within-donor slope [95% CI]` = fmt_sci(pooled, pooled_lo, pooled_hi),
                         `Heterogeneity F (4, G−1)` = het_F, `Heterogeneity p` = format(het_p, digits = 2),
                         `q (BH, regions)` = format(het_q, digits = 2),
                         `NeuN profile shift per SD regional AT8, L1 / L2 / L3 / L4 / L5–6` = shift,
                         `Layer × burden p` = format(burden_p, digits = 2),
                         `q ` = format(burden_q, digits = 2)) %>%
  show_table(caption = "Analysis C omnibus per region and donor set. Heterogeneity = equality of the five within-donor AT8-deviation → NeuN slopes (4 df). Layer × burden = whether the NeuN laminar profile shifts with regional AT8 burden (4 df). CR1 donor-cluster Wald; BH within each donor set across regions. NeuN measures immunoreactive profiles, not neuron number.")
lam_C %>% mutate(cell = fmt_sci(estimate, lo, hi), Layer = LAM_LAB[term]) %>%
  select(Variant = variant, Region = region, Layer, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Layer, values_from = cell) %>%
  show_table(caption = sprintf("Layer-specific within-donor AT8 → NeuN slopes (normal-score units: SD of NeuN per SD of AT8), donor-bootstrap 95%% CI (%d resamples). Display quantities; not tested one by one.", B_BOOT))
write_csv(lam_C %>% left_join(lam_C_omni %>% select(variant, region, het_q, burden_q), by = c("variant", "region")),
          file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_C_neun_coupling.csv"))
```

**Reading.** These are statements about **reduced NeuN immunoreactivity** (an altered neuronal
phenotype). Absolute neuronal loss is neither established nor excluded.

- **MTG: the within-donor AT8–NeuN association is layer-dependent** (heterogeneity q
  `r format(lc("MTG"), digits = 2)`).
  - **L2:** a donor's relative tau excess goes with relatively lower NeuN
    (`r lcs("MTG", "Layer2")` SD per SD).
  - **L5–6 and L4:** the association is positive (L5–6 `r lcs("MTG", "Layer5-6")`; L4
    `r lcs("MTG", "Layer4")`).
  - **Averaged over layers** the slopes cancel (pooled `r lcp("MTG")`). The single regional
    coefficient of Section 3.3 hides the depth structure.
  - **Robustness.** Heterogeneity holds without the `r sum(donor$severe)` severely affected
    donors (q `r format(lc("MTG", "het_q", "Without severely affected donors"), digits = 2)`) and
    without the two NeuN-floor donors (q
    `r format(lc("MTG", "het_q", "Without the 2 NeuN-floor donors"), digits = 2)`). Only the L1 slope
    changes materially (`r lcs("MTG", "Layer1")` with, `r lcs("MTG", "Layer1", "Without severely affected donors")`
    without them; Figure 4C, paired rows). The L2 and deep-layer readings are stable.
- **DFC: no supported depth dependence.** Heterogeneity q is `r format(lc("DFC"), digits = 2)`,
  and `r format(lc("DFC", "het_q", "Without severely affected donors"), digits = 2)` without the
  severely affected donors. The DFC point pattern is similar (negative upper and middle layers,
  positive deep layers), but it is not separable from noise.
- **NeuN profile shift with burden.** The NeuN laminar profile shifts with regional AT8 burden in
  MTG (q `r format(lc("MTG", "burden_q"), digits = 2)`; without severely affected donors
  `r format(lc("MTG", "burden_q", "Without severely affected donors"), digits = 2)`). In DFC
  (q `r format(lc("DFC", "burden_q"), digits = 2)`) it rests on the severely affected donors
  (`r format(lc("DFC", "burden_q", "Without severely affected donors"), digits = 2)` without them),
  but not on the two NeuN-floor donors alone
  (`r format(lc("DFC", "burden_q", "Without the 2 NeuN-floor donors"), digits = 2)`). That is the
  severe-phenotype pattern Section 5 found for donor-wide NeuN.
- **Why a positive deep-layer association is not protection.** AT8 % area is partly carried by the
  tau-bearing somata of the neurons that remain. Where more NeuN-immunoreactive neurons persist,
  there is more substrate for AT8, so a positive within-layer association is expected from
  measurement alone. The informative feature is the **contrast**: L2 behaves differently from
  the deep layers.
- **Layer bins are NeuN-defined.** The layer annotations come from a NeuN-trained classifier
  (Section 7.1). A NeuN laminar profile is therefore partly a property of how layers were drawn,
  which is one more reason to read these as covariation, not mechanism.

### 7.6 Analysis D — does the laminar profile add cognitive information?

**A prespecified 2 regions × 6 outcomes matrix**, ACT donors only. The outcomes are notebook 05's
cognitive family: terminal CASI and the released global, memory, executive, language and
visuospatial slopes.

**Models.**

- **Baseline:** `outcome (SD) ~ CPS_Global_pTau + regional AT8 + age + sex + education + timing`.
  Regional AT8 is the grey-matter normal score, Section 3's direct-AT8 scale. Timing is the CASI
  interval for terminal CASI and years from the last visit for the slopes, as in Section 4.3.
- **Laminar model:** baseline plus the region's AT8 laminar profile as one block: the centred
  log-ratio of L1–L4, the *K* − 1 = 4 sum-to-zero contrasts. Any full-rank contrast basis gives
  the same test and partial R².

**Reported per cell:**

- **cross-validated ΔR²**, the main summary of generalizable information (Figure 4D);
- the nested F test, and BH q across all 12 cells;
- partial R² of the block, with a donor-bootstrap interval, as a secondary descriptive.

**Why ΔR² and not partial R² leads.** Under the null, adding 4 terms to a model with 62 residual
df gives an expected partial R² of 4/62 ≈ 0.065, so in-sample partial R² is positively biased and
visually overstates evidence. Held-out ΔR² is centred near or below zero under the null.

**Cross-validation hygiene.**

- **Folds:** donor-level leave-one-out (69 folds) as primary, with 20 repeats of 10-fold CV as a
  stability check. Baseline and laminar models share identical folds.
- **No leakage:** the regional-AT8 normal score is recomputed within each training fold, and a
  held-out donor is scored against the training donors' distribution only. The clr profile uses
  only the donor's own five layers, so it needs no sample statistics. The outcome is modelled on
  its released scale (ΔR² is scale-free), so no outcome standardization enters prediction.
- **ΔR²** = (SSE_baseline − SSE_laminar) / Σ(y − training-fold mean)², pooled over held-out donors.

**Curvature sensitivity.** Notebook 05 kept linear global pTau as primary and found concave
curvature for terminal CASI and memory. The same single quadratic term is added to every cell as a
sensitivity, with its own BH family. There is no spline or threshold search.

**Follow-up rule (fixed in advance).** A per-layer coefficient plot is drawn only for a cell with
primary q < 0.05.

```{r}
#| label: laminar-cognition

LAM_OUT <- tibble(outcome = c("Terminal CASI", "Global decline", "Memory decline", "Executive decline",
                              "Language decline", "Visuospatial decline"),
                  var = c("casi", SLOPE_GLOBAL, DOMAINS$slope),
                  timing = c("casi_interval", rep("last_ybd", 5)))
lam_cog_data <- function(r) {
  prof <- lay %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>%
    transmute(donor_id, k = paste0("c", as.integer(layer)), clr) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = clr) %>%
    left_join(lam_gm %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% select(donor_id, at8_gm, at8_gm_ns), by = "donor_id")
  act %>% inner_join(prof, by = "donor_id")
}
LAM_BLOCK <- c("c1", "c2", "c3", "c4")

# --- fold-safe cross-validation -------------------------------------------------------
# Blom score of a held-out value against a training reference only (mid-rank as if inserted).
ns_against <- function(x, ref) {
  n <- length(ref)
  map_dbl(x, function(v) stats::qnorm((sum(ref < v) + 0.5 * sum(ref == v) + 0.5 - 3 / 8) / (n + 1 + 1 / 4)))
}
cv_checks <- list()
cv_dr2_folds <- function(d, fb, ff, folds) {
  sse_b <- sse_f <- sst <- 0
  for (f in unique(folds)) {
    te <- folds == f
    dtr <- d[!te, ]; dte <- d[te, ]
    dtr$at8_gm_cv <- normal_score(dtr$at8_gm)                 # training donors only
    dte$at8_gm_cv <- ns_against(dte$at8_gm, dtr$at8_gm)
    cv_checks[[length(cv_checks) + 1]] <<- !any(dte$donor_id %in% dtr$donor_id) && nrow(dtr) + nrow(dte) == nrow(d)
    mb <- lm(fb, dtr); mf <- lm(ff, dtr)                        # identical training rows for both
    sse_b <- sse_b + sum((dte$yraw - predict(mb, dte))^2)
    sse_f <- sse_f + sum((dte$yraw - predict(mf, dte))^2)
    sst <- sst + sum((dte$yraw - mean(dtr$yraw))^2)
  }
  (sse_b - sse_f) / sst
}
LAM_CV_REPEATS <- 20
lam_D <- pmap_dfr(expand_grid(region = LAM_REGIONS, LAM_OUT), function(region, outcome, var, timing) {
  d <- lam_cog_data(region) %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) %>% mutate(yz = zstd(.data[[var]]), yraw = .data[[var]])
  fb <- as.formula(paste("yz ~ CPS_Global_pTau + at8_gm_ns + age + sex + education +", timing))
  ff <- update(fb, paste(". ~ . +", paste(LAM_BLOCK, collapse = " + ")))
  fb_cv <- as.formula(paste("yraw ~ CPS_Global_pTau + at8_gm_cv + age + sex + education +", timing))
  ff_cv <- update(fb_cv, paste(". ~ . +", paste(LAM_BLOCK, collapse = " + ")))
  cv_loo <- cv_dr2_folds(d, fb_cv, ff_cv, seq_len(nrow(d)))
  set.seed(BOOT_SEED)
  cv_k10 <- replicate(LAM_CV_REPEATS, cv_dr2_folds(d, fb_cv, ff_cv, sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(d)))))
  base <- lm(fb, d); full <- lm(ff, d)
  baseq <- update(base, . ~ . + I(CPS_Global_pTau^2)); fullq <- update(full, . ~ . + I(CPS_Global_pTau^2))
  stopifnot("nested laminar models on identical donors" =
              nobs(base) == nobs(full) && nobs(baseq) == nobs(fullq) && nobs(full) == nrow(d))
  a <- anova(base, full); aq <- anova(baseq, fullq)
  pr2_fun <- function(x) {
    y <- x$yz; rb <- sum(.lm.fit(model.matrix(fb, x), y)$residuals^2)
    rf <- sum(.lm.fit(model.matrix(ff, x), y)$residuals^2); c(pr2 = (rb - rf) / rb)
  }
  bt <- cluster_bootstrap(d, pr2_fun, B_BOOT, seed = BOOT_SEED)
  tibble(region, outcome, n = nobs(full), resid_df = df.residual(full), F = a$F[2], p = a$`Pr(>F)`[2],
         pr2 = bt$estimate, pr2_lo = bt$lo, pr2_hi = bt$hi, n_boot_ok = bt$n_boot_ok,
         cv_dr2 = cv_loo, cv_k10_med = median(cv_k10), cv_k10_lo = min(cv_k10), cv_k10_hi = max(cv_k10),
         p_quad = aq$`Pr(>F)`[2], pr2_quad = (deviance(baseq) - deviance(fullq)) / deviance(baseq),
         null_pr2 = length(LAM_BLOCK) / df.residual(base))
}) %>% mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH"), q_quad = p.adjust(p_quad, "BH"),
              region = factor(region, levels = LAM_REGIONS), outcome = factor(outcome, levels = LAM_OUT$outcome))
stopifnot(
  "one prespecified family of 12 region x cognition cells" = nrow(lam_D) == 12L,
  "every cell uses the 69 ACT donors" = all(lam_D$n == 69L),
  "every bootstrap resample fitted" = all(lam_D$n_boot_ok == B_BOOT),
  "no region x cognition laminar block survives FDR" = all(lam_D$q >= 0.05),
  "CV: every held-out fold is disjoint from its training donors (12 cells x (69 LOO + 20 x 10) folds)" =
    length(cv_checks) == 12L * (69L + LAM_CV_REPEATS * 10L) && all(unlist(cv_checks)),
  "Figure 4D CV ΔR² unchanged from the frozen 2026-10-06 values (LOO, MTG then DFC, outcome order)" =
    max(abs(lam_D$cv_dr2 - c(0.043269, 0.036577, 0.004529, -0.067425, 0.027130, -0.077956,
                             -0.055029, -0.024396, -0.045306, -0.081242, -0.127373, -0.035785))) < 1e-6
)
ld <- function(r, o, col) lam_D[[col]][lam_D$region == r & lam_D$outcome == o]
lam_D_supported <- lam_D %>% filter(q < 0.05)
stopifnot(
  "every DFC cell worsens out-of-sample prediction" = all(lam_D$cv_dr2[lam_D$region == "DFC"] < 0),
  "MTG terminal CASI attenuates under the quadratic; MTG language does not survive its FDR" =
    ld("MTG", "Terminal CASI", "p_quad") > 0.05 && ld("MTG", "Language decline", "q_quad") >= 0.05
)

lam_D %>% transmute(Region = region, Outcome = outcome, Donors = n,
                    `F (4, df)` = sprintf("%.2f (4, %d)", F, resid_df),
                    `Partial R² [95% CI]` = fmt_ci(pr2, pr2_lo, pr2_hi, 3),
                    `CV ΔR² (LOO)` = sprintf("%+.3f", cv_dr2),
                    `CV ΔR², 10-fold × 20: median [range]` = sprintf("%+.3f [%+.3f, %+.3f]", cv_k10_med, cv_k10_lo, cv_k10_hi),
                    p = sprintf("%.3f", p), `q (BH, 12)` = sprintf("%.2f", q),
                    `+ quadratic: partial R²` = sprintf("%.3f", pr2_quad),
                    `+ quadratic: p` = sprintf("%.3f", p_quad), `+ quadratic: q` = sprintf("%.2f", q_quad)) %>%
  show_table(caption = sprintf("Analysis D. Laminar AT8 profile block (4 sum-to-zero contrasts) added to outcome ~ CPS_Global_pTau + regional AT8 + age + sex + education + timing, ACT donors. Partial R² interval: donor bootstrap (%d resamples; percentile intervals of a non-negative statistic are biased upward). Null expectation of partial R² = %.3f. CV ΔR² = (SSE_baseline − SSE_laminar) / held-out total SS on identical donor folds, with the regional-AT8 normal score re-estimated in each training fold; negative means the block worsens held-out prediction.", B_BOOT, lam_D$null_pr2[1]))
write_csv(lam_D, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_D_cognition.csv"))
```

**Reading.** **No region × cognition cell survives the prespecified FDR**: the minimum q is
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(lam_D$q))`, and no cell meets the follow-up rule, so no follow-up
coefficient plot is drawn.

- **Held-out prediction (Figure 4D).** Adding the laminar block changes held-out R² by
  `r sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", min(lam_D$cv_dr2), max(lam_D$cv_dr2))` across the 12 cells.
  - **DFC:** every cell is negative (`r sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", min(lam_D$cv_dr2[lam_D$region == "DFC"]), max(lam_D$cv_dr2[lam_D$region == "DFC"]))`):
    the depth profile worsens prediction. DFC executive decline gains nothing
    (ΔR² `r sprintf("%+.3f", ld("DFC", "Executive decline", "cv_dr2"))`, p
    `r sprintf("%.2f", ld("DFC", "Executive decline", "p"))`). The DFC–executive association of
    Sections 4.4–5 is carried by how much DFC tau a donor has, not by its depth distribution.
  - **MTG:** the largest gains are small: terminal CASI
    `r sprintf("%+.3f", ld("MTG", "Terminal CASI", "cv_dr2"))`, global decline
    `r sprintf("%+.3f", ld("MTG", "Global decline", "cv_dr2"))`, language decline
    `r sprintf("%+.3f", ld("MTG", "Language decline", "cv_dr2"))`. Repeated 10-fold CV spans zero for
    each of them (terminal CASI `r sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", ld("MTG", "Terminal CASI", "cv_k10_lo"), ld("MTG", "Terminal CASI", "cv_k10_hi"))`).
- **In-sample partial R² overstates this.** MTG terminal CASI has partial R²
  `r sprintf("%.2f", ld("MTG", "Terminal CASI", "pr2"))` (p `r sprintf("%.3f", ld("MTG", "Terminal CASI", "p"))`),
  against a null expectation of `r sprintf("%.3f", lam_D$null_pr2[1])` for four noise terms, yet it
  adds only a few hundredths of held-out R². Partial R² is kept as secondary text only.
- **Curvature sensitivity.**
  - The MTG–terminal CASI signal attenuates once Global pTau enters quadratically (p
    `r sprintf("%.2f", ld("MTG", "Terminal CASI", "p_quad"))`), as Section 5's DFC–CASI
    association did.
  - MTG–language strengthens (p `r sprintf("%.3f", ld("MTG", "Language decline", "p_quad"))`), but
    it does not survive that family's FDR (q
    `r sprintf("%.2f", ld("MTG", "Language decline", "q_quad"))`) and is a sensitivity, not a
    finding.
- **No anatomical specificity is claimed.** MTG's held-out ΔR² exceeds DFC's for
  `r sum(lam_D$cv_dr2[lam_D$region == "MTG"] > lam_D$cv_dr2[lam_D$region == "DFC"])` of 6 outcomes,
  with no single domain standing out. With 69 donors and a 4-df block, laminar AT8 shows substantial
  tissue organization but **little robust, generalizable cognitive information beyond regional
  burden**.

### 7.7 Figure 4

```{r}
#| label: fig4-build

# --- shared encodings ------------------------------------------------------------
# Diverging fills reuse Figure 2B's validated pair (blue / warm grey / orange-red).
# Orange reads "more tau than expected" (A) or "more tau, less NeuN" (C); in D the pair is
# re-labelled worse / better held-out prediction in its own legend.
DIV_NEG <- "#1c5cab"; DIV_MID <- "#f4f3ef"; DIV_POS <- "#c2410c"
GP_LOW <- "#eef3fa"; GP_HIGH <- "#0d366b"               # Global pTau: notebook 05's blue ramp
LAM_P_LIM <- 1.5                                       # log2; ~99th percentile of |P|
lay_lab <- function(x) factor(LAM_LAB[as.character(x)], levels = rev(LAM_LAB))   # L1 drawn on top
cell_text <- function(v, lim) if_else(abs(v) > 0.55 * lim, "white", INK)
heat_theme <- theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
                    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
                    legend.key.width = unit(6, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(2.4, "mm"))
fmt_q <- function(q) if_else(q < 0.001, "q < 0.001", sprintf("q = %.2g", q))
fmt_p <- function(p) map_chr(p, ~ if (.x < 0.001) sprintf("p = %.0e", .x) else sprintf("p = %.2g", .x))

# --- A. global progression -> regional AT8 -> relative laminar AT8 -----------------------
# One donor order for every row: ascending CPS_Global_pTau.
gp_order <- donor$donor_id[order(donor$CPS_Global_pTau)]
gp_sorted <- donor$CPS_Global_pTau[match(gp_order, donor$donor_id)]
tert_sorted <- donor$gp_tertile[match(gp_order, donor$donor_id)]
tert_n <- cumsum(table(tert_sorted))[1:2]
tert_cut <- unname(tert_n) + 0.5
gp_q <- quantile(donor$CPS_Global_pTau, c(1/3, 2/3))
n_don <- length(gp_order)
x_of <- function(ids) match(ids, gp_order)
a_rows <- list(
  gp = tibble(donor_id = gp_order, x = seq_len(n_don), CPS_Global_pTau = gp_sorted),
  burden = lam_gm %>% filter(brain_region %in% LAM_REGIONS) %>% mutate(x = x_of(donor_id)),
  profile = lay %>% mutate(x = x_of(donor_id))
)
stopifnot(
  "Figure 4A: donors ordered by ascending Global pTau" = all(diff(gp_sorted) >= 0),
  "Figure 4A: tertile boundaries fall exactly between the ordered Global pTau tertiles" =
    !is.unsorted(as.integer(tert_sorted)) &&
    all(gp_sorted[seq_len(tert_n[1])] <= gp_q[1]) && all(gp_sorted[-seq_len(tert_n[1])] > gp_q[1]) &&
    all(gp_sorted[seq_len(tert_n[2])] <= gp_q[2]) && all(gp_sorted[-seq_len(tert_n[2])] > gp_q[2]),
  "Figure 4A: the Global pTau strip is monotone left to right" =
    all(diff(a_rows$gp$CPS_Global_pTau[order(a_rows$gp$x)]) >= 0),
  "Figure 4A: MTG and DFC rows use the identical donor order, one column per donor" =
    all(map_lgl(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
      b <- a_rows$burden %>% filter(brain_region == r); p <- a_rows$profile %>% filter(brain_region == r)
      setequal(b$x, seq_len(n_don)) && !anyDuplicated(b$x) && setequal(p$x, seq_len(n_don)) &&
        all(gp_order[b$x] == b$donor_id) && all(gp_order[p$x] == p$donor_id)
    }))
)
a_x <- scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(0), limits = c(0.5, n_don + 0.5))
a_vlines <- geom_vline(xintercept = tert_cut, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "22")
strip_theme <- heat_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(1, 8, 0, 8),
                                  plot.title = element_text(size = rel(0.95), margin = margin(b = 1)))
gp_strip <- ggplot(a_rows$gp, aes(x, "Global pTau", fill = CPS_Global_pTau)) +
  geom_tile(height = 0.9) + a_vlines + a_x +
  annotate("text", x = c(tert_cut[1] / 2, mean(tert_cut), (tert_cut[2] + n_don + 0.5) / 2), y = 1.62,
           label = c("low", "mid", "high Global pTau tertile"), size = 2.3, family = FIG_FONT,
           colour = INK2, vjust = 0) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = GP_LOW, high = GP_HIGH, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1),
                      name = "Global pTau (CPS_Global_pTau)") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + strip_theme + theme(plot.margin = margin(12, 8, 2, 8))
burden_strip <- function(r) {
  ggplot(a_rows$burden %>% filter(brain_region == r), aes(x, "Regional AT8", fill = burden)) +
    geom_tile(height = 0.9) + a_vlines + a_x +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = HEAT_LOW, high = HEAT_HIGH, limits = range(lam_gm$burden),
                        breaks = log2(c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10)), labels = c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10"),
                        name = "Regional AT8 (grey matter, % area)") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = r) + strip_theme
}
profile_heat <- function(r, x_axis = FALSE) {
  ggplot(a_rows$profile %>% filter(brain_region == r) %>% mutate(L = lay_lab(layer)), aes(x, L, fill = P)) +
    geom_tile() + a_vlines + a_x +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = DIV_NEG, mid = DIV_MID, high = DIV_POS, midpoint = 0,
                         limits = c(-LAM_P_LIM, LAM_P_LIM), oob = squish, na.value = MISSING,
                         breaks = c(-1.5, 0, 1.5), labels = c("≤ −1.5", "0", "≥ +1.5"),
                         name = "Relative laminar AT8 (log2)") +
    labs(x = if (x_axis) sprintf("%d donors, ordered by CPS_Global_pTau (lowest → highest); same order in every row", n_don) else NULL,
         y = "pial ↓ deep") +
    heat_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(0, 8, 2, 8),
                       axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(0.8), colour = INK2))
}
f4a_body <- plot_grid(
  gp_strip + no_legend,

# --- C. AT8-NeuN laminar covariation, all donors and without SA ---------------------------
```
