  labs(title = "AT8–NeuN laminar\ncovariation", x = "pial → deep", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Within donor, comparable burden;\nrow q = layer heterogeneity") +
  heat_theme + theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(0.8), colour = INK2),
                     axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 0.9),
                     strip.text = element_text(margin = margin(t = 2, b = 1)))

# --- D. held-out cognitive information of the laminar block ---------------------------------
D_COLS <- c(`Terminal CASI` = "Term.\nCASI", `Global decline` = "Global", `Memory decline` = "Mem-\nory",
            `Executive decline` = "Exec-\nutive", `Language decline` = "Lan-\nguage",
            `Visuospatial decline` = "Visuo-\nspatial")
f4d_d <- lam_D %>% mutate(col = factor(D_COLS[as.character(outcome)], levels = D_COLS),
                          row = factor(paste0(region, "\nn = ", n), levels = rev(paste0(LAM_REGIONS, "\nn = ", n[match(LAM_REGIONS, region)]))),
                          supported = q < 0.05)
D_LIM <- 0.1
f4d <- ggplot(f4d_d, aes(col, row, fill = cv_dr2)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_tile(data = f4d_d %>% filter(supported), fill = NA, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.3f", cv_dr2), colour = cell_text(cv_dr2, D_LIM)),
            size = 2.1, family = FIG_FONT, vjust = -0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("pR² %.2f", pr2), colour = if_else(abs(cv_dr2) > 0.55 * D_LIM, "white", INK2)),
            size = 1.6, family = FIG_FONT, vjust = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = DIV_POS, mid = DIV_MID, high = DIV_NEG, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-D_LIM, D_LIM),
                       oob = squish, breaks = c(-0.1, 0, 0.1), labels = c("−0.1\nworse", "0", "+0.1\nbetter"),
                       name = "Held-out\nΔR²") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(title = "Cognitive information\nbeyond burden", x = "terminal level · rates of decline", y = NULL,
       subtitle = sprintf("Held-out CV ΔR² (pR² = in-sample\npartial R²); min q = %.2f, 12 cells", min(lam_D$q))) +
  heat_theme + theme(axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 0.9),
                     axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(0.8), colour = INK2))

small_leg <- theme(legend.key.width = unit(4.2, "mm"), plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 6, 6))
f4c <- f4c + small_leg; f4d <- f4d + small_leg; f4b <- f4b + theme(plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 6, 6))
fig4 <- plot_grid(
  compose(f4a, labels = "A"),
  compose(f4b, f4c, f4d, labels = c("B", "C", "D"), nrow = 1, align = "h", axis = "b",
          rel_widths = c(1.25, 0.95, 1.25)),
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1.3, 1)
)
fig4_png <- save_figure(fig4, "fig4_multiregional_laminar_pathology", height_mm = 200)

fig4_cap <- sprintf(paste0(
  "**Figure 4. Regional burden and cortical-depth organization in the two layer-resolved neocortical regions (MTG, DFC).** ",
  "**A** Global progression → regional burden → relative laminar AT8, for the %d donors (columns) in one order, ascending CPS_Global_pTau, shared by every row. Top strip: CPS_Global_pTau itself (monotone by construction); dashed lines and labels = its all-donor tertiles. Regional AT8 strips: each region's grey-matter AT8, which varies around the global trajectory and is allowed to be non-monotone. Heatmaps: the relative laminar profile P (rows L1 at the pial surface to L5–6) = log2 of the layer's AT8 relative to the region's grey-matter value, minus that layer's cohort mean; orange = more AT8 in that layer than the donor's regional burden and the typical laminar distribution imply; clipped at ±%.1f log2; no layer value is missing. A relative decrease is not an absolute one: absolute AT8 rises in every layer (Supplementary Figure S4A). The hierarchy is descriptive, not causal. ",
  "**B** Equal-layer cumulative normalized layer-mean AT8 signal from deep (L5–6) to superficial: each layer's mean %% AT8 area divided by the sum over the five layers, layers weighted equally. The four intermediate boundaries carry the information; the final + L1 point equals 1 by construction (muted). Curves are derived from the continuous clr ~ CPS_Global_pTau model and evaluated at the tertile medians (anchors, not groups); bands = donor-bootstrap 95%% intervals. Facet p = 4-df layer × Global pTau test (donor fixed effects, CR1); subtitle = direct region × layer × Global pTau test on %d donors with both regions, clustered on donor. For MTG the area-weighted section contribution (released layer areas) is a different estimand and is given alongside; DFC has no released layer areas. Not a fraction of total cortical tau or a cortical-column trajectory: the released layer summaries keep no local pial-to-white-matter geometry. ",
  "**C** Within-donor association between a layer's AT8 deviation and its NeuN-immunoreactive density at comparable regional burden (normal-score SD units), with all donors and without the %d published severely affected (SA) donors. Row q = 4-df layer-heterogeneity test (BH across regions within donor set). Reduced NeuN immunoreactivity is an altered neuronal phenotype; absolute neuronal loss is neither established nor excluded; positive deep-layer associations are neither protective nor evidence of neuron preservation. ",
  "**D** Donor-level cross-validated ΔR² from adding the 4-contrast AT8 laminar block to outcome ~ CPS_Global_pTau + regional AT8 + age + sex + education + timing (%d ACT donors; leave-one-out on identical folds for both models, regional-AT8 normal score re-estimated in each training fold). Small text = in-sample partial R² (null expectation %.3f). Outlines would mark q < 0.05 across the 12-cell family; none qualify. ",
  "Cross-sectional associations; not causal."),

fig5s_cap <- sprintf(paste0(

**Title choice.** Panel D provides no FDR-supported or held-out cognitive evidence, so the figure
is titled for tissue organization ("regional burden and cortical-depth organization"). It does
not link laminar tau to cognitive heterogeneity.

### 7.8 Beyond AT8 and beyond cortical layers: a bounded audit for Figure 5

Two questions, each answered only if the June 2026 workbook supports it:

- **A.** Is the progression-related cortical-depth reorganization specific to tau, or part of a
  broader laminar tissue-response phenotype (MTG/DFC, other layer-resolved QNP families)?
- **B.** Outside the neocortical layer system, does progression alter the internal anatomical
  distribution of pathology beyond total regional burden (HIP subfields, MEC subdivisions)?

Neither runs any cognition model, and neither reproduces SEA-AD's MTG IBA1–amyloid analysis.

**A. Layer-resolved QNP families in MTG and DFC.** Selection rules, fixed before any progression
model: one metric per stain family; full five-layer coverage; mostly non-zero; an amount that can
distribute across depth (not a per-cell size or shape); a documented classifier.

```{r}
#| label: qnp-layer-inventory

lam_cols <- map_dfr(LAM_REGIONS, function(r) {
  d <- qnp_raw[[r]] %>% filter(`analysis region` %in% LAM_LAYERS)
  map_dfr(setdiff(names(d), QNP_ID_COLS), function(cn) {
    v <- d[[cn]]
    tibble(region = r, metric = cn,
           donors_complete = d %>% group_by(`Donor ID`) %>% summarise(ok = sum(!is.na(.data[[cn]])) == 5, .groups = "drop") %>% pull(ok) %>% sum(),
           zero_frac = mean(v == 0, na.rm = TRUE))
  })
})
LAM_MARKERS <- tribble(
  ~marker,              ~metric,                                     ~family,
  "AT8 (pTau)",         "percent AT8 positive area",                 "pTau (AT8)",
  "6E10 (Aβ)",          "percent 6e10 positive area",                "Aβ (6E10)",
  "IBA1 cells",         "number of Iba1 positive cells per area",    "microglia (IBA1)",
  "GFAP",               "percent GFAP positive area",                "astrocytes (GFAP)",
  "NeuN cells",         "number of NeuN positive cells per area",    "neurons (NeuN)",
  "Hematoxylin nuclei", "number of Hematoxylin positive nuclei per area", "all nuclei (hematoxylin)"
)
lam_inv <- lam_cols %>%
  mutate(stain = case_when(str_detect(metric, "AT8") ~ "AT8", str_detect(metric, "pTDP43") ~ "pTDP-43",
                           str_detect(metric, "6e10.*Iba1|Iba1.*6e10") ~ "6E10 × IBA1",
                           str_detect(metric, "6e10") ~ "6E10", str_detect(metric, "Iba1") ~ "IBA1",
                           str_detect(metric, "GFAP") ~ "GFAP", str_detect(metric, "NeuN") ~ "NeuN",
                           str_detect(metric, "Hematoxylin") ~ "Hematoxylin", str_detect(metric, "aSyn") ~ "α-syn",
                           TRUE ~ "other")) %>%
  group_by(stain, metric) %>%
  summarise(regions = paste(region[donors_complete == 84], collapse = " + "),
            donors = paste(donors_complete, collapse = " / "),
            zero = paste(if_else(is.nan(zero_frac), "–", percent(zero_frac, 1)), collapse = " / "),
            max_zero = max(zero_frac, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(role = case_when(
    metric %in% LAM_MARKERS$metric ~ "selected (Figure 5A)",
    regions != "MTG + DFC" ~ "excluded: not released in both regions",
    stain %in% c("pTDP-43", "α-syn") ~ "excluded: mostly zero (sparse co-pathology)",
    stain == "6E10 × IBA1" ~ "excluded: derived two-stain colocalization",
    str_detect(metric, "activated|inactivated") ~ "excluded: undocumented activation classifier",
    str_detect(metric, "^average") ~ "excluded: per-cell/object size or shape, not an amount across depth",
    TRUE ~ "excluded: redundant with the selected metric of the same stain"))
stopifnot(
  "one selected metric per stain family, each with all 84 donors in both regions" =
    nrow(filter(lam_inv, role == "selected (Figure 5A)")) == nrow(LAM_MARKERS) &&
    all(filter(lam_inv, role == "selected (Figure 5A)")$regions == "MTG + DFC") &&
    all(filter(lam_inv, role == "selected (Figure 5A)")$max_zero < 0.1),
  "sparse co-pathology stains are excluded by the zero rule" =
    all(filter(lam_inv, stain %in% c("pTDP-43", "α-syn"))$max_zero > 0.5)
)
lam_inv %>% arrange(role != "selected (Figure 5A)", stain, metric) %>%
  transmute(Stain = stain, Metric = metric, `Regions with 5 layers × 84 donors` = regions,
            `Donors, MTG / DFC` = donors, `Zero layer values, MTG / DFC` = zero, Role = role) %>%
  show_table(caption = "Every layer-resolved QNP metric in the June 2026 MTG and DFC tabs. Layer bins are the same registered annotations for every stain (a NeuN-trained classifier propagated by serial-section registration), so layer definitions are compatible across families.")
write_csv(lam_inv, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_qnp_family_inventory.csv"))
```

**Eligibility for Figure 5A.** Six distinct stain families (pTau, Aβ, microglia, astrocytes,
neurons, all nuclei) are layer-resolved in both regions for all 84 donors on compatible,
registered layer bins. That is enough for a coherent comparison, so Figure 5A is drawn.

**Model.** For every marker the cumulative normalized layer-mean signal *C* (Section 7.2) is
built exactly as for AT8. A linear-scale share is used because 6E10 has zero layers (a donor with
no signal in any layer has no profile and is dropped from that marker). One 4-df test of the
four non-terminal boundaries against continuous Global pTau per marker × region (CR1), with BH
across the 6 × 2 = 12 tests. The fill is the standardized slope (SD of the cumulative share per SD
of Global pTau); positive means a larger share in the deeper bins at higher progression.

```{r}
#| label: laminar-markers

mk_long <- pmap_dfr(expand_grid(region = LAM_REGIONS, LAM_MARKERS), function(region, marker, metric, family) {
  qnp_raw[[region]] %>% filter(`analysis region` %in% LAM_LAYERS) %>%
    transmute(donor_id = `Donor ID`, brain_region = region, marker,
              layer = factor(`analysis region`, levels = LAM_LAYERS), at8 = .data[[metric]])
}) %>% left_join(donor %>% transmute(donor_id, gz = zstd(CPS_Global_pTau)), by = "donor_id")
mk_dropped <- mk_long %>% group_by(brain_region, marker, donor_id) %>% summarise(tot = sum(at8), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(tot == 0)
mk_cum <- mk_long %>% anti_join(mk_dropped, by = c("brain_region", "marker", "donor_id")) %>%
  group_by(marker) %>% group_modify(~ cum_build(.x)) %>% ungroup()
lam_mk <- mk_cum %>% group_by(brain_region, marker) %>% group_modify(~ cum_test(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  rename(region = brain_region)
lam_mk_omni <- lam_mk %>% distinct(region, marker, n, F, df2, p, pillai_p) %>% mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH"))
lam_mk <- lam_mk %>% left_join(lam_mk_omni %>% select(region, marker, q), by = c("region", "marker"))
lmk <- function(r, m, col = "q") lam_mk_omni[[col]][lam_mk_omni$region == r & lam_mk_omni$marker == m]
stopifnot(
  "one omnibus per marker x region: a family of 12" = nrow(lam_mk_omni) == 12L,
  "every marker profile terminates at 1 and every donor kept has signal" =
    all(abs(mk_cum$C[mk_cum$k == 5] - 1) < 1e-12) && all(lam_mk_omni$n >= 80),
  "the AT8 row reproduces the Section 7.4 cumulative test" =
    all(abs(map_dbl(LAM_REGIONS, ~ lmk(.x, "AT8 (pTau)", "p")) - map_dbl(LAM_REGIONS, lct)) < 1e-12)
)
lam_mk_omni %>% arrange(region, q) %>%
  transmute(Region = region, Marker = marker, Donors = n, `F (4, G−1)` = F,
            p = format(p, digits = 2), `q (BH, 12)` = format(q, digits = 2),
            `Pillai p` = format(pillai_p, digits = 2)) %>%
  show_table(caption = sprintf("Figure 5A omnibus: does the cumulative depth profile of each marker change with continuous Global pTau? Donors dropped for an all-zero profile: %s.",
                               if (nrow(mk_dropped)) paste(sprintf("%s %s %s", mk_dropped$brain_region, mk_dropped$marker, mk_dropped$donor_id), collapse = "; ") else "none"))
write_csv(lam_mk, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_5A_marker_depth_progression.csv"))
mk_sig <- function(r) lam_mk_omni %>% filter(region == r, q < 0.05) %>% pull(marker)
stopifnot(
  "DFC: AT8 is the only marker whose depth profile changes with progression (as stated)" =
    identical(mk_sig("DFC"), "AT8 (pTau)"),
  "MTG: several non-tau markers pass FDR, with GFAP deeper and 6E10/IBA1 more superficial (as stated)" =
    all(c("GFAP", "6E10 (Aβ)", "IBA1 cells") %in% mk_sig("MTG")) &&
    mean(lam_mk$std[lam_mk$region == "MTG" & lam_mk$marker == "GFAP"]) > 0 &&
    mean(lam_mk$std[lam_mk$region == "MTG" & lam_mk$marker == "6E10 (Aβ)"]) < 0 &&
    mean(lam_mk$std[lam_mk$region == "MTG" & lam_mk$marker == "IBA1 cells"]) < 0
)
```

**Two follow-ups, each one prespecified family.**

- **Does MTG's multimarker pattern persist when layer area is incorporated?** For all six
  prespecified marker families, the area-weighted section contribution is tested the same way,
  using that marker's own slide areas (released, never inferred). BH across exactly these six,
  with no selection by the equal-layer results. Severe-donor exclusion is reported for both
  estimands.
- **Do MTG and DFC differ?** For each of the six markers, the direct region × boundary ×
  Global pTau test on donors with a valid profile in both regions (stacked cumulative curves,
  CR1 clustered on donor; Pillai on the per-donor DFC − MTG difference as cross-check). BH across
  the six.

```{r}
#| label: laminar-markers-area-direct

# --- area-weighted section contribution, all six prespecified MTG markers ---------------------
MK_AREA_SLIDE <- c(`AT8 (pTau)` = "AT8 and pTDP43", `6E10 (Aβ)` = "Iba1 and 6e10", `IBA1 cells` = "Iba1 and 6e10",
                   GFAP = "GFAP", `NeuN cells` = "NeuN", `Hematoxylin nuclei` = "Hematoxylin")
mk_area_set <- LAM_MARKERS$marker                  # fixed by the inventory, not by any result
mk_area_long <- mk_long %>% filter(brain_region == "MTG", marker %in% mk_area_set) %>%
  mutate(slide = unname(MK_AREA_SLIDE[marker])) %>%
  left_join(mtg_area %>% select(donor_id, slide, layer, area), by = c("donor_id", "slide", "layer")) %>%
  left_join(donor %>% select(donor_id, severe), by = "donor_id") %>%
  anti_join(mk_dropped, by = c("brain_region", "marker", "donor_id"))
gab_vals <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(LAM_MARKERS)), function(i) map_dfr(LAM_LAYERS, ~ tibble(
  donor_id = gab$`Donor ID`, marker = LAM_MARKERS$marker[i], layer = factor(.x, levels = LAM_LAYERS),
  v_gab = gab[[paste0(LAM_MARKERS$metric[i], "_", .x)]])))
mk_area_chk <- mk_area_long %>% left_join(gab_vals, by = c("donor_id", "marker", "layer"))
stopifnot(
  "area-weighted BH family = exactly the six prespecified markers; no result-based selection" =
    identical(mk_area_set, LAM_MARKERS$marker) && length(mk_area_set) == 6L,
  "area-weighted analysis uses real released areas for every MTG donor x layer, and is MTG only" =
    !anyNA(mk_area_long$area) && all(mk_area_long$brain_region == "MTG"),
  "the deprecated tab's marker values equal the June MTG values (densities rounded to 7 decimals there)" =
    !anyNA(mk_area_chk$v_gab) && max(abs(mk_area_chk$at8 - mk_area_chk$v_gab)) <= 5e-8 + 1e-12
)
mk_area_one <- function(d, weight = NULL) cum_test(cum_build(d, weight))
lam_mk_area <- map_dfr(mk_area_set, function(m) {
  d <- mk_area_long %>% filter(marker == m)
  eq <- mk_area_one(d); aw <- mk_area_one(d, "area")
  eq_sa <- mk_area_one(d %>% filter(!severe)); aw_sa <- mk_area_one(d %>% filter(!severe), "area")
  tibble(marker = m, n = eq$n[1], p_eq = eq$p[1], p_aw = aw$p[1], p_eq_nosa = eq_sa$p[1], p_aw_nosa = aw_sa$p[1],
         std_eq = list(eq$std), std_aw = list(aw$std))
}) %>% mutate(q_aw = p.adjust(p_aw, "BH")) %>%
  left_join(lam_mk_omni %>% filter(region == "MTG") %>% select(marker, q_eq = q), by = "marker")
stopifnot("area-weighted equal-layer p reproduces the Figure 5A MTG test" =
            all(abs(lam_mk_area$p_eq - map_dbl(lam_mk_area$marker, ~ lmk("MTG", .x, "p"))) < 1e-12))
pattern_of <- function(v) if (all(v > 0)) "deeper-weighted" else if (all(v < 0)) "more superficial" else "mixed by boundary"
lam_mk_area <- lam_mk_area %>% mutate(pat_eq = map_chr(std_eq, pattern_of), pat_aw = map_chr(std_aw, pattern_of),
                                      area_support = q_aw < 0.05)

# --- direct MTG vs DFC region x boundary x Global pTau, six markers ------------------------------
mk_direct_one <- function(m) {
  z <- mk_cum %>% filter(marker == m, k < 5)
  both <- z %>% distinct(donor_id, brain_region) %>% count(donor_id) %>% filter(n == 2) %>% pull(donor_id)
  z <- z %>% filter(donor_id %in% both) %>% mutate(isD = as.numeric(brain_region == "DFC"))
  Bk <- diag(4)[z$k, ]
  o <- cr_wald(cbind(Bk * (1 - z$isD), Bk * z$isD, Bk * z$gz * (1 - z$isD), Bk * z$gz * z$isD),
               z$C, z$donor_id, 1:16, R = cbind(matrix(0, 4, 8), -diag(4), diag(4)))
  wm <- z %>% filter(brain_region == "MTG") %>% select(donor_id, k, C, gz) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = C) %>% arrange(donor_id)
  wd <- z %>% filter(brain_region == "DFC") %>% select(donor_id, k, C) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = C) %>% arrange(donor_id)
  stopifnot("direct test pairs each donor's own MTG and DFC profiles" = identical(wm$donor_id, wd$donor_id) && nrow(wm) == length(both))
  tibble(marker = m, n = length(both), F = o$F, df2 = o$df2, p = o$p,
         pillai_p = anova(lm(as.matrix(wd[as.character(1:4)]) - as.matrix(wm[as.character(1:4)]) ~ wm$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2])
}
lam_mk_dir <- map_dfr(LAM_MARKERS$marker, mk_direct_one) %>% mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH"))
lmd <- function(m, col = "q") lam_mk_dir[[col]][lam_mk_dir$marker == m]
lma <- function(m, col = "q_aw") lam_mk_area[[col]][lam_mk_area$marker == m]
stopifnot(
  "the regional-difference BH family is exactly the six Figure 5A markers" =
    nrow(lam_mk_dir) == 6L && setequal(lam_mk_dir$marker, LAM_MARKERS$marker),
  "every donor contributes to both regions except all-zero 6E10 profiles" =
    all(lam_mk_dir$n[lam_mk_dir$marker != "6E10 (Aβ)"] == 84L) && lmd("6E10 (Aβ)", "n") >= 80L,
  "stated pattern: AT8, GFAP and 6E10 differ between regions; IBA1, NeuN and nuclei do not" =
    setequal(lam_mk_dir$marker[lam_mk_dir$q < 0.05], c("AT8 (pTau)", "GFAP", "6E10 (Aβ)")),
  "stated pattern: area-weighted support for 6E10, GFAP, NeuN and nuclei; not for IBA1 or AT8" =
    setequal(lam_mk_area$marker[lam_mk_area$area_support], c("6E10 (Aβ)", "GFAP", "NeuN cells", "Hematoxylin nuclei")) &&
    lmk("MTG", "Hematoxylin nuclei") >= 0.05
)
lam_mk_area %>% left_join(lam_mk_dir %>% select(marker, q_dir = q), by = "marker") %>%
  transmute(Marker = marker, Donors = n,
            `Equal-layer p (q, 12-test family)` = sprintf("%s (%s)", format(p_eq, digits = 2), format(q_eq, digits = 2)),
            `Equal-layer pattern` = pat_eq,
            `Area-weighted p (q, BH over 6)` = sprintf("%s (%s)", format(p_aw, digits = 2), format(q_aw, digits = 2)),
            `Area-weighted pattern` = pat_aw,
            `Without SA: equal-layer / area-weighted p` = sprintf("%s / %s", format(p_eq_nosa, digits = 2), format(p_aw_nosa, digits = 2)),
            `MTG ≠ DFC q` = format(q_dir, digits = 2)) %>%
  show_table(caption = "MTG: equal-layer concentration profile versus area-weighted section contribution for all six prespecified markers (BH across the six area-weighted tests). Each marker is area-weighted with its own slide's released layer areas. Pattern = sign of the standardized slopes across the four deep → superficial boundaries. The two estimands answer different questions; neither is a check on the other.")
lam_mk_dir %>% transmute(Marker = marker, Donors = n, `F (4, G−1)` = sprintf("%.2f (4, %d)", F, df2),
                         p = format(p, digits = 2), `q (BH, 6)` = format(q, digits = 2), `Pillai p (paired difference)` = format(pillai_p, digits = 2)) %>%
  show_table(caption = "Direct MTG versus DFC test per marker: region × boundary × Global pTau on stacked equal-layer cumulative curves, CR1 clustered on donor. 6E10 drops donors whose layer profile is all zero in either region.")
write_csv(lam_mk_area %>% mutate(std_eq = map_chr(std_eq, ~ paste(sprintf("%.3f", .x), collapse = " ")),
                                 std_aw = map_chr(std_aw, ~ paste(sprintf("%.3f", .x), collapse = " "))),
          file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_5A_MTG_equal_vs_area_weighted.csv"))
write_csv(lam_mk_dir, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "laminar_5A_region_difference.csv"))
```

**Reading (5A).**

- **DFC: a comparatively selective AT8 depth phenotype.** Among the six measured QNP families,
  only AT8 showed FDR-supported progression-associated cortical-depth reorganization (q
  `r format(lmk("DFC", "AT8 (pTau)"), digits = 2)`). 6E10, IBA1, GFAP, NeuN and nuclear density do
  not (smallest other q `r format(min(lam_mk_omni$q[lam_mk_omni$region == "DFC" & lam_mk_omni$marker != "AT8 (pTau)"]), digits = 2)`).
  No between-marker interaction model is fitted, so this is selectivity among the measured
  families, not formal tau specificity.
- **MTG: a broader multimarker pattern.** `r paste(mk_sig("MTG"), collapse = ", ")` pass FDR in
  MTG, where AT8 itself is at the margin (q `r format(lmk("MTG", "AT8 (pTau)"), digits = 2)` on this
  scale). GFAP becomes deeper-weighted; 6E10 and IBA1 more superficially weighted.
- **Which effects differ between regions.** The direct test supports a regional difference for
  AT8 (q `r format(lmd("AT8 (pTau)"), digits = 2)`), GFAP (`r format(lmd("GFAP"), digits = 2)`) and
  6E10 (`r format(lmd("6E10 (Aβ)"), digits = 2)`), not for IBA1 (`r format(lmd("IBA1 cells"), digits = 2)`),
  NeuN (`r format(lmd("NeuN cells"), digits = 2)`) or nuclei (`r format(lmd("Hematoxylin nuclei"), digits = 2)`).
  So MTG's IBA1 and NeuN effects, though FDR-supported within MTG, are not shown to differ from DFC.
- **Which MTG effects persist with layer area incorporated** (all six markers, BH across six). In
  the area-weighted section contribution, 6E10 (q `r format(lma("6E10 (Aβ)"), digits = 2)`), GFAP
  (`r format(lma("GFAP"), digits = 2)`) and NeuN (`r format(lma("NeuN cells"), digits = 2)`) remain
  supported, IBA1 does not (`r format(lma("IBA1 cells"), digits = 2)`), and AT8 keeps its direction
  without support (`r format(lma("AT8 (pTau)"), digits = 2)`).
- **Nuclei show what geometry alone does.** Hematoxylin nuclear density has no equal-layer depth
  change (q `r format(lmk("MTG", "Hematoxylin nuclei"), digits = 2)`) but its area-weighted section
  contribution does change (q `r format(lma("Hematoxylin nuclei"), digits = 2)`). Nuclear density is
  roughly even across layers, so its section contribution mostly follows the classifier-derived
  layer-area fractions. This makes nuclei an internal reference: an area-weighted change can arise
  from changing layer geometry with no change in concentration. A marker whose area-weighted pattern
  is supported is therefore not, on that basis alone, reorganizing biologically.
- **NeuN changes shape.** NeuN stays supported but its pattern differs between estimands: standardized
  slopes at the four boundaries are `r paste(sprintf("%+.2f", lma("NeuN cells", "std_eq")[[1]]), collapse = " ")`
  equal-layer and `r paste(sprintf("%+.2f", lma("NeuN cells", "std_aw")[[1]]), collapse = " ")`
  area-weighted, so for NeuN the geometry changes what the section-level distribution looks like.
- **What this means.** The 6E10 and GFAP depth changes are the most coherent MTG tissue-depth
  findings: supported in the equal-layer concentration profile, in the section contribution, and
  different from DFC. The IBA1 effect depends on equal layer weighting; NeuN's shape and the nuclei
  result depend on how geometry is handled. MTG's layer
  bins are drawn by a NeuN-trained classifier whose area fractions change with progression, so
  every MTG layer result carries that caveat. DFC, the strongest result, shows no multimarker
  pattern.

**B. Internal anatomical subdivisions outside MTG/DFC.**

```{r}
#| label: anat-subdivisions

hm_raw <- qnp_raw[["Hip-MEC"]] %>% filter(`analysis region` != "Grey matter") %>%
  transmute(donor_id = `Donor ID`, region = `brain region`, analysis_region = `analysis region`,
            compartment = str_remove(analysis_region, "-[LR]$"), side = str_extract(analysis_region, "[LR]$"),
            at8 = .data[[LAM_AT8]], ab = `percent 6e10 positive area`, neun = .data[[LAM_NEUN]],
            gfap = `percent GFAP positive area`, iba1 = `number of Iba1 positive cells per area`)
anat_gm <- qnp_raw[["Hip-MEC"]] %>% filter(`analysis region` == "Grey matter") %>%
  transmute(donor_id = `Donor ID`, region = `brain region`, at8_gm = .data[[LAM_AT8]])
anat_audit <- hm_raw %>% group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(Compartments = paste(unique(compartment), collapse = ", "),
            Hemispheres = paste(sort(unique(side)), collapse = "/"),
            n_comp = n_distinct(compartment),
            `Donors with every compartment (AT8, either side)` =
              sum(tapply(compartment[!is.na(at8)], donor_id[!is.na(at8)], n_distinct) == n_distinct(compartment)),
            `Stains at compartment level` = paste(c("AT8", "6E10", "NeuN", "GFAP", "IBA1")[c(any(!is.na(at8)), any(!is.na(ab)), any(!is.na(neun)), any(!is.na(gfap)), any(!is.na(iba1)))], collapse = ", "),
            `Zero AT8 values` = sum(at8 == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(anat_gm %>% group_by(region) %>% summarise(`Whole-region AT8 donors` = sum(!is.na(at8_gm))), by = "region") %>%
  mutate(Decision = if_else(n_comp >= 3 & `Donors with every compartment (AT8, either side)` >= LAM_MIN_DONORS,
                            "eligible: internal anatomical distribution",
                            "not eligible: one subdivision type split by hemisphere; no internal distribution"))
ANAT_ELIGIBLE <- anat_audit$region[str_detect(anat_audit$Decision, "^eligible")]
stopifnot("HIP is the only eligible non-neocortical internal anatomy; MEC is not" = identical(ANAT_ELIGIBLE, "HIP"))
anat_audit %>% select(-n_comp) %>% rename(Region = region) %>%
  show_table(caption = "Internal anatomical subdivisions in the June 2026 Hip-MEC tab (L/R = left/right, per the QNP documentation). EC appears as a compartment of the hippocampal section. No other tab has sub-regional units.")

# HIP: AT8 per subfield, averaged over the available hemispheres on the log scale.
HIP_COMP <- c("EC", "Sub", "CA1", "CA2", "CA3", "CA4", "DG")
hip <- hm_raw %>% filter(region == "HIP", !is.na(at8)) %>%
  group_by(donor_id, compartment) %>% summarise(y = mean(log2(at8 + LAM_LOG_OFFSET)), n_side = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(donor_id) %>% filter(n() == length(HIP_COMP)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = HIP_COMP)) %>%
  left_join(donor %>% transmute(donor_id, gz = zstd(CPS_Global_pTau), CPS_Global_pTau, severe), by = "donor_id") %>%
  left_join(anat_gm %>% filter(region == "HIP") %>% transmute(donor_id, bz = zstd(log2(at8_gm + LAM_LOG_OFFSET))), by = "donor_id") %>%
  group_by(donor_id) %>% mutate(clr = y - mean(y)) %>% ungroup() %>% arrange(donor_id, compartment)
HIP_CS <- contr.sum(length(HIP_COMP))
hip_omni <- function(d, expo = "gz") {
  L <- HIP_CS[as.integer(d$compartment), ]
  cr_wald(demean_by(cbind(L, L * d[[expo]]), d$donor_id), d$y - ave(d$y, d$donor_id), d$donor_id, 7:12)
}
hip_w <- hip %>% select(donor_id, compartment, clr, gz, CPS_Global_pTau) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = clr)
hip_res <- tibble(
  n = nrow(hip_w), F = hip_omni(hip)$F, df1 = 6L, df2 = hip_omni(hip)$df2, p = hip_omni(hip)$p,
  pillai_p = anova(lm(as.matrix(hip_w[HIP_COMP[1:6]]) ~ hip_w$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2],
  p_no_sa = hip_omni(hip %>% filter(!severe))$p, p_burden = hip_omni(hip %>% filter(!is.na(bz)), "bz")$p,
  both_sides = sum(tapply(hip$n_side, hip$donor_id, min) == 2))
hip_vc <- variance_components(hip %>% mutate(lyr = compartment), "y", roi = "lyr")
hip_slopes <- setNames(map_dbl(HIP_COMP, ~ unname(coef(lm(hip_w[[.x]] ~ hip_w$gz))[2])), HIP_COMP)
# Hemisphere replicate: per-side clr profiles agree within donor?
hip_lr <- hm_raw %>% filter(region == "HIP", !is.na(at8)) %>% group_by(donor_id, side) %>% filter(n() == length(HIP_COMP)) %>%
  mutate(c = log2(at8 + LAM_LOG_OFFSET) - mean(log2(at8 + LAM_LOG_OFFSET))) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(donor_id, compartment, side, c) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = side, values_from = c) %>% drop_na() %>%
  group_by(compartment) %>% summarise(rho = cor(L, R, method = "spearman"), .groups = "drop")
# Absolute versus relative: standardized slope (Pearson r with Global pTau) of each compartment's
# absolute log2 AT8, and of its normalized compartment share s = 2^y / sum(2^y) (equal weight per
# compartment; y = hemisphere-averaged log2 AT8). Shares sum to 1 per donor, so relative changes
# are constrained to offset one another.
hip_share <- hip %>% group_by(donor_id) %>% mutate(s = 2^y / sum(2^y)) %>% ungroup()
hip_ar_w <- hip_share %>% select(donor_id, compartment, abs = y, rel = s, gz) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = c(abs, rel))
hip_ar_stat <- function(w) unlist(map(names(ABSREL), function(k)
  setNames(map_dbl(HIP_COMP, ~ cor(w[[paste0(k, "_", .x)]], w$gz)), paste0(k, "_", HIP_COMP))))
hip_absrel <- cluster_bootstrap(hip_ar_w, hip_ar_stat, B_BOOT, seed = BOOT_SEED) %>%
  separate(term, c("rep", "compartment"), sep = "_") %>%
  mutate(representation = unname(ABSREL[rep]), compartment = factor(compartment, levels = HIP_COMP))
hip_abs_p <- anova(lm(as.matrix(hip_ar_w[paste0("abs_", HIP_COMP)]) ~ hip_ar_w$gz))$`Pr(>F)`[2]
har <- function(c, k = "Absolute") hip_absrel$estimate[hip_absrel$compartment == c & hip_absrel$representation == k]

# Left/right: hemispheres are never separate donors. QC = (i) within-donor agreement of the two
# hemispheres' clr profiles, (ii) the progression test refitted on each hemisphere alone.
hip_side <- hm_raw %>% filter(region == "HIP", !is.na(at8)) %>% group_by(donor_id, side) %>%
  filter(n() == length(HIP_COMP)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = HIP_COMP), y = log2(at8 + LAM_LOG_OFFSET)) %>%
  left_join(donor %>% transmute(donor_id, gz = zstd(CPS_Global_pTau)), by = "donor_id") %>%
  group_by(donor_id, side) %>% mutate(clr = y - mean(y)) %>% ungroup() %>% arrange(side, donor_id, compartment)
hip_lr_donor <- hip_side %>% select(donor_id, compartment, side, clr) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = side, values_from = clr) %>% drop_na() %>%
  group_by(donor_id) %>% filter(n() == length(HIP_COMP)) %>% summarise(r = cor(L, R), .groups = "drop")
hip_by_side <- map_dfr(c("L", "R"), function(sd_) {
  d <- hip_side %>% filter(side == sd_)
  w <- d %>% select(donor_id, compartment, clr, gz) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = clr)
  tibble(side = sd_, n = n_distinct(d$donor_id), p = hip_omni(d)$p, compartment = HIP_COMP,
         slope = map_dbl(HIP_COMP, ~ unname(coef(lm(w[[.x]] ~ w$gz))[2])))
})
hsd <- function(sd_, col = "p") hip_by_side[[col]][hip_by_side$side == sd_][1]
stopifnot(
  "HIP: every donor kept has all seven compartments" = all(count(hip, donor_id)$n == length(HIP_COMP)) && hip_res$n >= LAM_MIN_DONORS,
  "HIP: hemispheres averaged within donor, one row per donor x compartment (never independent donors)" =
    !anyDuplicated(hip[c("donor_id", "compartment")]) && all(hip$n_side %in% 1:2) &&
    n_distinct(hip$donor_id) == hip_res$n,
  "HIP normalized compartment shares are bounded and sum to 1 per donor" =
    all(hip_share$s > 0 & hip_share$s < 1) && max(abs(tapply(hip_share$s, hip_share$donor_id, sum) - 1)) < 1e-12,
  "every bootstrap resample fitted" = all(hip_absrel$n_boot_ok == B_BOOT),
  "HIP: absolute AT8 rises in every compartment (as stated)" =
    all(hip_absrel$lo[hip_absrel$representation == "Absolute"] > 0),
  "HIP: the redistribution is present in each hemisphere alone, same direction for EC (-) and CA3/CA4 (+)" =
    hsd("L") < 0.05 && hsd("R") < 0.05 &&
    all(hip_by_side %>% filter(compartment == "EC") %>% pull(slope) < 0) &&
    all(hip_by_side %>% filter(compartment %in% c("CA3", "CA4")) %>% pull(slope) > 0),
  "HIP compartment x Global pTau is supported and survives SA exclusion" = hip_res$p < 0.05 && hip_res$p_no_sa < 0.05,
  "HIP: EC, Sub and CA1 lose relative share and CA3, CA4 gain it with progression (as stated)" =
    all(hip_slopes[c("EC", "Sub", "CA1")] < 0) && all(hip_slopes[c("CA3", "CA4")] > 0),
  "HIP: left/right profile agreement is lowest in EC and CA1 (as stated)" =
    setequal(as.character(hip_lr$compartment[order(hip_lr$rho)][1:2]), c("EC", "CA1"))
)
hip_res %>% transmute(Region = "HIP", Donors = n, `Both hemispheres` = both_sides,
                      `Compartment × Global pTau F` = sprintf("%.2f (%d, %d)", F, df1, df2), p = format(p, digits = 2),
                      `Pillai p` = format(pillai_p, digits = 2), `Without SA p` = format(p_no_sa, digits = 2),
                      `Indexed by HIP burden p` = format(p_burden, digits = 2),
                      `Burden / compartment / donor × compartment variance` =
                        paste(percent(hip_vc$share[match(c("donor", "ROI", "donor x ROI"), hip_vc$component)], 1), collapse = " / ")) %>%
  show_table(caption = "HIP AT8: does the internal subfield distribution change with continuous Global pTau beyond each donor's overall hippocampal AT8 level? Donor fixed effects absorb that level; 6-df compartment × progression block, CR1 donor-cluster Wald. Compartment values are log2 AT8 averaged over the available hemispheres.")
write_csv(anat_audit, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "anatomical_subdivision_audit.csv"))
write_csv(bind_rows(hip_res %>% mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>% pivot_longer(everything()),
                    tibble(name = paste0("clr_slope_per_SD_", HIP_COMP), value = sprintf("%.4f", hip_slopes)),
                    tibble(name = paste0("LR_rho_", hip_lr$compartment), value = sprintf("%.3f", hip_lr$rho))),
          file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "anatomical_HIP_progression.csv"))
write_csv(hip_absrel, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "anatomical_HIP_absolute_vs_relative.csv"))
write_csv(hip_by_side, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "anatomical_HIP_by_hemisphere.csv"))
tibble(Check = c("Within-donor L/R clr-profile Pearson r, median [IQR]",
                 "Per-compartment L/R Spearman ρ (range)",
                 "Compartment × Global pTau, left only", "Compartment × Global pTau, right only"),
       Result = c(sprintf("%.2f [%.2f–%.2f], %d donors", median(hip_lr_donor$r), quantile(hip_lr_donor$r, 0.25), quantile(hip_lr_donor$r, 0.75), nrow(hip_lr_donor)),
                  sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(hip_lr$rho), max(hip_lr$rho)),
                  sprintf("p = %s (%d donors); slopes EC→DG %s", format(hsd("L"), digits = 2), hsd("L", "n"), paste(sprintf("%+.2f", hip_by_side$slope[hip_by_side$side == "L"]), collapse = " ")),
                  sprintf("p = %s (%d donors); slopes EC→DG %s", format(hsd("R"), digits = 2), hsd("R", "n"), paste(sprintf("%+.2f", hip_by_side$slope[hip_by_side$side == "R"]), collapse = " ")))) %>%
  show_table(caption = "HIP left/right concordance (QC only; hemispheres are averaged within donor in every model). Slopes = clr log2 per SD of Global pTau.")
hs <- function(c) sprintf("%+.2f", hip_slopes[[c]])
```

**Reading (5B).**

- **MEC is not eligible.** Its only subdivision is TEC, split by hemisphere (left/right). A
  two-hemisphere split is not an internal anatomical distribution, so MEC is not modelled.
- **HIP is eligible** (`r hip_res$n` donors with all seven compartments; `r hip_res$both_sides`
  with both hemispheres). It is analysed on its own anatomical axis, never as layers.
- **Progression changes the HIP subfield distribution.** Compartment × Global pTau F
  `r sprintf("%.1f", hip_res$F)` on (6, `r hip_res$df2`) df, p `r format(hip_res$p, digits = 2)`
  (Pillai `r format(hip_res$pillai_p, digits = 2)`; without SA donors
  `r format(hip_res$p_no_sa, digits = 2)`; indexed by hippocampal burden
  `r format(hip_res$p_burden, digits = 2)`). At higher progression EC (`r hs("EC")` log2 per SD),
  Sub (`r hs("Sub")`) and CA1 (`r hs("CA1")`) become relatively lower within the normalized
  compartment-mean AT8 profile, and CA3 (`r hs("CA3")`) and CA4 (`r hs("CA4")`) relatively higher.
- **Absolute AT8 rises everywhere** (Figure 5B, left). Every compartment's absolute AT8 increases
  with Global pTau (standardized slopes
  `r sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(hip_absrel$estimate[hip_absrel$representation == "Absolute"]), max(hip_absrel$estimate[hip_absrel$representation == "Absolute"]))`;
  joint p `r format(hip_abs_p, digits = 2)`). EC becoming relatively lower in the normalized
  profile (`r sprintf("%+.2f", har("EC", "Relative"))` standardized) therefore means EC rises less
  steeply than CA3/CA4 (`r sprintf("%+.2f", har("CA3", "Relative"))`, `r sprintf("%+.2f", har("CA4", "Relative"))`),
  not that EC pathology declines.
- **What the normalized profile is.** Each compartment's mean AT8 divided by the sum over the seven
  compartments, giving every compartment equal representational status. No compartment areas or
  volumes are released, so it is **not** a fraction of total hippocampal pathology or a tau
  allocation. Its values sum to 1, so relative increases and decreases are constrained to offset
  each other.
- **Not a temporal sequence.** The compartment order (EC, Sub, CA1–CA4, DG) is anatomical. The
  pattern is consistent with classical hippocampal staging, but this cross-sectional association
  does not show pathology moving between compartments.
- **Burden still dominates.** As in cortex, the donor (burden) component carries
  `r percent(hip_vc$share[hip_vc$component == "donor"], 1)` of log subfield AT8 variance,
  compartment baselines `r percent(hip_vc$share[hip_vc$component == "ROI"], 1)`, and the
  donor × compartment remainder `r percent(hip_vc$share[hip_vc$component == "donor x ROI"], 1)`.
- **Left and right agree; averaging is reasonable.** Hemispheres are averaged within donor and
  never counted as separate donors. A donor's left and right clr profiles correlate with median
  r `r sprintf("%.2f", median(hip_lr_donor$r))` (IQR `r sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", quantile(hip_lr_donor$r, 0.25), quantile(hip_lr_donor$r, 0.75))`).
  Across donors, single-compartment agreement is lower (Spearman ρ
  `r sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(hip_lr$rho), max(hip_lr$rho))`, lowest in EC and CA1). The progression
  redistribution is present in each hemisphere alone (left p `r format(hsd("L"), digits = 2)`, right p
  `r format(hsd("R"), digits = 2)`), with the same EC-down, CA3/CA4-up direction. No laterality
  analysis is pursued.

Figure 5B is therefore drawn for HIP only.

```{r}
#| label: fig5-build

# --- A. multimarker cumulative-depth atlas ------------------------------------------------
# Tiles: standardized slope per boundary. Two indicator columns, one glyph each:
#   "MTG ≠ DFC"  direct region x boundary x pTau test (BH over 6), same in both facets;
#   "area-wtd"   MTG only, area-weighted section contribution (BH over the tested markers).
A5_IND <- c("MTG ≠\nDFC", "area-\nweighted")
A5_X <- c(CUM_LAB[1:4], A5_IND)
f5a_d <- lam_mk %>% mutate(bin = factor(CUM_LAB[k], levels = A5_X),

f5a_ind <- bind_rows(
  f5a_rows %>% left_join(lam_mk_dir %>% select(marker, q_dir = q), by = "marker") %>%

stopifnot("Figure 5A indicators: six regional-difference glyphs per facet; area glyphs only for tested MTG markers" =
            sum(f5a_ind$bin == A5_IND[1]) == 12L && all(f5a_ind$region[f5a_ind$bin == A5_IND[2]] == "MTG") &&

A5_LIM <- 0.6
f5a <- ggplot(f5a_d, aes(bin, row, fill = std)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +

                       breaks = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5), labels = c("−0.5\nmore superficial", "0", "+0.5\nmore deep"),

### 7.9 Spatial molecular depth information: readiness note only

No molecular analysis is run here. Three kinds of "laminar" molecular information must not be
confused:

1. **True spatial depth** (cell coordinates relative to pia in an intact section; MERFISH/Xenium).
2. **Layer-named cell types in dissociated snRNA-seq** (L2/3 IT, L4 IT, L5 ET, L6 IT …): canonical
   identities, not measurements of preserved cortical depth.
3. **Donor × region pseudobulk:** no depth at all.

Only category 1 is spatial laminar molecular information. Inspected read-only (HDF5 `obs` keys,
2026-10-06; not re-read at render because the r-quarto env has no HDF5 reader):

**Readiness.** True spatial cortical-depth molecular data are local for **MTG only** (MERFISH,
27 donors, normalized pial depth and layer labels). They could later give a local, depth-resolved
reference for the MTG laminar results here, but they cover a third of the cohort, one region, and
not DFC, where the progression-depth result is strongest.

### 7.10 Hippocampal burden, internal profile and the full cognitive phenotype (Figure 6)

**Question.** Across terminal cognition and the five released decline rates, how much information
is added first by **HIP-associated regional AT8 burden**, and then by the **internal compartment
profile**, beyond Global pTau progression? The profile is one hypothesis unit; no compartment is
tested on its own.

**Variables.**

- **HIP burden:** the released HIP **grey-matter** AT8 (% area), the whole-region value of the
  Hip-MEC tab. It is close to an area-weighted aggregate of the 14 compartment values (Section 7.8
  audit), so it is the regional total, not a sum of compartment concentrations. It enters on
  Section 3's direct-AT8 scale: a normal score across donors.
- **HIP profile:** the clr of the seven hemisphere-averaged compartment log2 AT8 values (EC, Sub,
  CA1, CA2, CA3, CA4, DG), expressed in an orthonormal ilr basis: exactly *K* − 1 = 6 contrasts.
  The inferential target is the 6-df block; it is invariant to the basis, and individual ilr
  coordinates are never interpreted.

**Models** (ACT donors with a complete HIP profile; outcome in SD; covariates and timing exactly
as in Sections 4.3–5 and 7.6):

- **M0:** `outcome ~ CPS_Global_pTau + age + sex + education + timing`
- **M1:** M0 + HIP-associated regional burden: does it add information?
- **M2:** M1 + HIP profile block: does internal organization add information beyond burden?

**Reported per outcome and increment (M1 − M0, M2 − M1):** nested F test, partial R², held-out
ΔR² (the primary practical quantity), donor N, and the same increment with a quadratic Global pTau
term (Notebook 05's established curvature sensitivity). **One family:** 2 increments × 6 outcomes =
12 tests, BH. **CV:** the Figure 4D framework: donor-level leave-one-out and 20 × 10-fold, with
identical folds for M0, M1 and M2, and the HIP-burden normal score re-estimated in each training
fold. The clr/ilr profile uses only each donor's own seven values and needs no training statistics.

```{r}
#| label: hip-cognition

HIP_ILR <- ilr_basis(length(HIP_COMP))
HIP_PROF_TERMS <- paste0("hz", seq_len(ncol(HIP_ILR)))
hip_prof <- hip %>% select(donor_id, compartment, clr) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = clr)
hip_Z <- as.matrix(hip_prof[HIP_COMP]) %*% HIP_ILR
colnames(hip_Z) <- HIP_PROF_TERMS
hip_burden <- anat_gm %>% filter(region == "HIP") %>%
  transmute(donor_id, hip_at8 = at8_gm, hip_ns = normal_score(at8_gm))
hip_cog_base <- act %>%
  inner_join(bind_cols(hip_prof %>% select(donor_id), as_tibble(hip_Z)), by = "donor_id") %>%
  inner_join(bind_cols(hip_prof %>% select(donor_id), as_tibble(as.matrix(hip_prof[HIP_COMP[-length(HIP_COMP)]])) %>%
                         rename_with(~ paste0("hc", seq_along(.x)))), by = "donor_id") %>%
  left_join(hip_burden, by = "donor_id")
stopifnot(
  "HIP profile: hemispheres averaged within donor, one profile per donor" =
    !anyDuplicated(hip_prof$donor_id) && !anyDuplicated(hip[c("donor_id", "compartment")]),
  "HIP profile has exactly K - 1 = 6 independent, orthonormal contrasts" =
    ncol(HIP_ILR) == length(HIP_COMP) - 1L && max(abs(crossprod(HIP_ILR) - diag(ncol(HIP_ILR)))) < 1e-12 &&
    base::qr(cbind(1, hip_Z))$rank == length(HIP_COMP) && max(abs(rowSums(hip_prof[HIP_COMP]))) < 1e-10,
  "every HIP-cognition donor has a burden value" = !anyNA(hip_cog_base$hip_at8)
)

# One CV pass fits every nested model on the same folds; `prep` builds any fold-dependent predictor
# from the training rows only.
cv_nested <- function(d, forms, folds, prep) {
  sse <- setNames(numeric(length(forms)), names(forms)); sst <- 0; ok <- TRUE
  for (f in unique(folds)) {
    te <- folds == f
    pp <- prep(d[!te, , drop = FALSE], d[te, , drop = FALSE])
    ok <- ok && !any(pp$test$donor_id %in% pp$train$donor_id) && nrow(pp$train) == sum(!te) && isTRUE(pp$train_only)
    for (m in names(forms)) {
      fit <- lm(forms[[m]], pp$train)
      sse[m] <- sse[m] + sum((pp$test$yraw - predict(fit, pp$test))^2)
    }
    sst <- sst + sum((pp$test$yraw - mean(pp$train$yraw))^2)
  }
  list(sse = sse, sst = sst, ok = ok)
}
hip_prep <- function(tr, te) {
  tr$hip_cv <- normal_score(tr$hip_at8)                 # training donors only
  te$hip_cv <- ns_against(te$hip_at8, tr$hip_at8)
  list(train = tr, test = te, train_only = TRUE)
}
cv_increments <- function(d, forms, prep, pairs) {
  loo <- cv_nested(d, forms, seq_len(nrow(d)), prep)
  set.seed(BOOT_SEED)
  k10 <- replicate(LAM_CV_REPEATS, {
    r <- cv_nested(d, forms, sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(d))), prep)
    c(ok = r$ok, map_dbl(pairs, ~ (r$sse[.x[1]] - r$sse[.x[2]]) / r$sst))
  })
  list(loo = map_dbl(pairs, ~ (loo$sse[.x[1]] - loo$sse[.x[2]]) / loo$sst),
       k10 = k10[-1, , drop = FALSE], ok = loo$ok && all(k10["ok", ] == 1))
}
HIP_PAIRS <- list(Burden = c("M0", "M1"), Profile = c("M1", "M2"))
hip_cv_ok <- logical(0)
hip_cog <- pmap_dfr(LAM_OUT, function(outcome, var, timing) {
  d <- hip_cog_base %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) %>% mutate(y = zstd(.data[[var]]), yraw = .data[[var]])
  base <- paste("CPS_Global_pTau + age + sex + education +", timing)
  f <- list(M0 = as.formula(paste("y ~", base)),
            M1 = as.formula(paste("y ~", base, "+ hip_ns")),
            M2 = as.formula(paste("y ~", base, "+ hip_ns +", paste(HIP_PROF_TERMS, collapse = " + "))))
  m <- map(f, ~ lm(.x, d))
  mq <- map(f, ~ lm(update(.x, . ~ . + I(CPS_Global_pTau^2)), d))
  stopifnot("nested HIP models on identical donors" = n_distinct(map_int(c(m, mq), nobs)) == 1L && nobs(m$M2) == nrow(d))
  # basis invariance: the first K - 1 clr coordinates give the same profile-block test
  m2c <- lm(as.formula(paste("y ~", base, "+ hip_ns +", paste0("hc", 1:6, collapse = " + "))), d)
  stopifnot("profile-block test is invariant to the contrast basis" =
              abs(anova(m$M1, m$M2)$F[2] - anova(m$M1, m2c)$F[2]) < 1e-8)
  fcv <- list(M0 = as.formula(paste("yraw ~", base)),
              M1 = as.formula(paste("yraw ~", base, "+ hip_cv")),
              M2 = as.formula(paste("yraw ~", base, "+ hip_cv +", paste(HIP_PROF_TERMS, collapse = " + "))))
  cv <- cv_increments(d, fcv, hip_prep, HIP_PAIRS)
  hip_cv_ok <<- c(hip_cv_ok, cv$ok)
  map_dfr(names(HIP_PAIRS), function(inc) {
    pr <- HIP_PAIRS[[inc]]; a <- anova(m[[pr[1]]], m[[pr[2]]]); aq <- anova(mq[[pr[1]]], mq[[pr[2]]])
    tibble(outcome, increment = inc, n = nrow(d), df1 = a$Df[2], df2 = a$Res.Df[2], F = a$F[2], p = a$`Pr(>F)`[2],
           pr2 = (deviance(m[[pr[1]]]) - deviance(m[[pr[2]]])) / deviance(m[[pr[1]]]),
           cv_dr2 = unname(cv$loo[inc]), cv_k10_med = median(cv$k10[inc, ]),
           cv_k10_lo = min(cv$k10[inc, ]), cv_k10_hi = max(cv$k10[inc, ]), p_quad = aq$`Pr(>F)`[2])
  })
}) %>% mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH"), increment = factor(increment, levels = names(HIP_PAIRS)),
              outcome = factor(outcome, levels = LAM_OUT$outcome))
hip_prof_supported <- hip_cog %>% filter(increment == "Profile", q < 0.05, cv_dr2 > 0.01)
stopifnot(
  "HIP cognition family = 2 increments x 6 outcomes = 12 tests, one BH family" =
    nrow(hip_cog) == 12L && setequal(as.character(hip_cog$outcome), LAM_OUT$outcome),
  "identical folds across M0/M1/M2 and training-only preprocessing in every fold" =
    length(hip_cv_ok) == 6L && all(hip_cv_ok),
  "burden is 1 df and the profile block is 6 df" =
    all(hip_cog$df1[hip_cog$increment == "Burden"] == 1L) && all(hip_cog$df1[hip_cog$increment == "Profile"] == 6L),
  "no compartment is tested on its own unless the profile block is supported" =
    nrow(hip_prof_supported) > 0 || !exists("hip_comp_cog")
)
# Human-readable compartment coefficients, only for supported profile blocks.
hip_prof_coef <- map_dfr(as.character(hip_prof_supported$outcome), function(o) {
  i <- match(o, LAM_OUT$outcome)
  d <- hip_cog_base %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[LAM_OUT$var[i]]])) %>% mutate(y = zstd(.data[[LAM_OUT$var[i]]]))
  fit <- lm(as.formula(paste("y ~ CPS_Global_pTau + age + sex + education +", LAM_OUT$timing[i], "+ hip_ns +",
                             paste(HIP_PROF_TERMS, collapse = " + "))), d)
  tibble(outcome = o, compartment = factor(HIP_COMP, levels = HIP_COMP), clr_coef = drop(HIP_ILR %*% coef(fit)[HIP_PROF_TERMS]))
})
hc <- function(o, inc, col) hip_cog[[col]][hip_cog$outcome == o & hip_cog$increment == inc]
stopifnot("stated result: no HIP burden or profile increment survives the 12-test FDR; no profile block supported" =
            all(hip_cog$q >= 0.05) && nrow(hip_prof_supported) == 0L)
hip_cog %>% transmute(Outcome = outcome, Increment = if_else(increment == "Burden", "M1 − M0: HIP burden", "M2 − M1: HIP profile (6 df)"),
                      Donors = n, `F (df)` = sprintf("%.2f (%d, %d)", F, df1, df2), p = sprintf("%.3f", p),
                      `q (BH, 12)` = sprintf("%.2f", q), `Partial R²` = sprintf("%.3f", pr2),
                      `CV ΔR² (LOO)` = sprintf("%+.3f", cv_dr2),
                      `CV ΔR², 10-fold × 20: median [range]` = sprintf("%+.3f [%+.3f, %+.3f]", cv_k10_med, cv_k10_lo, cv_k10_hi),
                      `+ quadratic Global pTau: p` = sprintf("%.3f", p_quad)) %>%
  arrange(Increment, Outcome) %>%
  show_table(caption = "Hippocampal pathology and cognition: nested increments beyond Global pTau and Notebook 05 covariates, ACT donors with a complete HIP profile. Burden = HIP grey-matter AT8 normal score (1 df); profile = 6 ilr contrasts of the hemisphere-averaged compartment clr. BH across all 12 tests. CV ΔR² on identical donor folds for M0–M2, with the burden normal score re-estimated in each training fold.")
write_csv(hip_cog, file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "hip_cognition_increments.csv"))
```

**Reading.**

- **HIP burden adds no supported information** beyond Global pTau for any outcome (smallest q
  `r sprintf("%.2f", min(hip_cog$q[hip_cog$increment == "Burden"]))`; held-out ΔR²
  `r sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", min(hip_cog$cv_dr2[hip_cog$increment == "Burden"]), max(hip_cog$cv_dr2[hip_cog$increment == "Burden"]))`).
  Memory, the outcome with the strongest anatomical prior, is no exception (q
  `r sprintf("%.2f", hc("Memory decline", "Burden", "q"))`, ΔR²
  `r sprintf("%+.3f", hc("Memory decline", "Burden", "cv_dr2"))`).
- **The internal HIP profile adds no supported information** beyond burden (smallest q
  `r sprintf("%.2f", min(hip_cog$q[hip_cog$increment == "Profile"]))`; held-out ΔR²
  `r sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", min(hip_cog$cv_dr2[hip_cog$increment == "Profile"]), max(hip_cog$cv_dr2[hip_cog$increment == "Profile"]))`).
  With 6 df on about `r min(hip_cog$n)` donors, in-sample partial R² for the profile
  (`r sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(hip_cog$pr2[hip_cog$increment == "Profile"]), max(hip_cog$pr2[hip_cog$increment == "Profile"]))`)
  sits near the null expectation of about `r sprintf("%.2f", 6 / min(hip_cog$df2[hip_cog$increment == "Profile"]))`.
- **No compartment follow-up.** No profile block met the prespecified rule (q < 0.05 with positive
  held-out ΔR²), so no compartment coefficients are shown or searched.
- **Curvature sensitivity.** With a quadratic Global pTau term in every model, the smallest
  unadjusted p is `r sprintf("%.3f", min(hip_cog$p_quad))`
  (`r with(hip_cog[which.min(hip_cog$p_quad), ], paste(as.character(outcome), tolower(as.character(increment))))`
  increment), which would not survive the same 12-test correction (BH min q
  `r sprintf("%.2f", min(p.adjust(hip_cog$p_quad, "BH")))`).
- **Reading.** Hippocampal AT8 changes its within-region pattern with progression (Section 7.8),
  but at n ≈ `r min(hip_cog$n)` neither the HIP-associated regional burden nor an arbitrary 6-df
  internal profile carries generalizable cognitive information beyond Global pTau. Section 9.3
  asks the narrower 1-df question this block may have been underpowered for: whether the one
  pathology-defined direction along which the profile changes with progression carries
  information.

```{r}
#| label: fig6-build

# --- A. anatomical context: absolute and relative compartment change (from Section 7.8) ----------
f6a_d <- hip_absrel %>% mutate(row = factor(if_else(representation == "Absolute", "Absolute AT8", "Relative profile"),
                                            levels = c("Relative profile", "Absolute AT8")))
f6a <- ggplot(f6a_d, aes(compartment, row, fill = estimate)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.2f", estimate), colour = cell_text(estimate, 1)), size = 2.1, family = FIG_FONT) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = DIV_NEG, mid = DIV_MID, high = DIV_POS, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1),
                       breaks = c(-1, 0, 1), labels = c("−1", "0", "+1"), name = "SD per SD\nGlobal pTau") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(title = "HIP AT8 across progression",
       subtitle = "Standardized slopes; relative = normalized\ncompartment-mean profile (Figure 5B)", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  heat_theme + theme(legend.key.width = unit(4.2, "mm"))

# --- B, C. held-out information added by burden, then by the internal profile --------------------
f6_row <- function(inc, title, subtitle) {
  d <- hip_cog %>% filter(increment == inc) %>%
    mutate(col = factor(D_COLS[as.character(outcome)], levels = D_COLS), row = sprintf("n = %d", n))
  ggplot(d, aes(col, row, fill = cv_dr2)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = d %>% filter(q < 0.05), fill = NA, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.3f", cv_dr2), colour = cell_text(cv_dr2, D_LIM)), size = 2.1, family = FIG_FONT, vjust = -0.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("pR² %.2f · q %.2f", pr2, q), colour = if_else(abs(cv_dr2) > 0.55 * D_LIM, "white", INK2)),
              size = 1.6, family = FIG_FONT, vjust = 1.4) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = DIV_POS, mid = DIV_MID, high = DIV_NEG, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-D_LIM, D_LIM),
                         oob = squish, breaks = c(-0.1, 0, 0.1), labels = c("−0.1\nworse", "0", "+0.1\nbetter"), name = "Held-out\nΔR²") +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    heat_theme + theme(axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 0.9), legend.key.width = unit(4.2, "mm"))
}
f6b <- f6_row("Burden", "Information added by HIP-associated regional burden (M1 − M0)",
              "Held-out CV ΔR²; small text = in-sample partial R² and q (BH, 12 tests)")
f6c <- f6_row("Profile", "Information added by the internal HIP profile (M2 − M1, 6 df)",
              "Held-out CV ΔR²; small text = in-sample partial R² and q (BH, 12 tests)")

# --- D. supported profile coefficients, or a CV-stability diagnostic when none is supported -------
if (nrow(hip_prof_coef)) {
  f6d <- ggplot(hip_prof_coef, aes(compartment, clr_coef)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +

} else {
  f6d_d <- hip_cog %>% mutate(o = factor(as.character(outcome), levels = rev(LAM_OUT$outcome)),
                              inc = if_else(increment == "Burden", "Burden (M1 − M0)", "Profile (M2 − M1)"))
  f6d_dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.55)

f6b <- f6b + no_legend
fig6 <- plot_grid(
  plot_grid(f6a, f6d, labels = c("A", "D"), label_size = 10, label_fontfamily = FIG_FONT, label_fontface = "bold",

B and C: donor-level leave-one-out on identical folds for M0–M2, burden normal score re-estimated in each training fold; %d ACT donors; small text = in-sample partial R² and BH q across the 12 tests; outlines would mark q < 0.05 (none). ",

### 7.11 Targeted conventional-stage sensitivities

Conventional stages are used only where they match the measurement, and only as sensitivities:

- **DFC AT8 depth profile × Braak** (Section 7.4);
- **HIP AT8 compartment profile × Braak:** the Section 7.8 donor fixed-effects model with ordered
  Braak stage in place of Global pTau;
- **MTG 6E10 depth profile × Thal phase and × CERAD score:** the equal-layer cumulative curve of
  Figure 5A, with the ordered stage in place of Global pTau. These are two prespecified amyloid
  sensitivities. ADNC is a composite and is not used.

```{r}
#| label: stage-sensitivities

stage_tbl <- donor_meta %>%
  transmute(donor_id = `Donor ID`,
            braak_num = as.integer(factor(str_remove(Braak, "Braak "), levels = c("0", "I", "II", "III", "IV", "V", "VI"))) - 1L,
            thal_num = as.integer(str_extract(Thal, "[0-9]")),
            cerad_num = match(`CERAD score`, c("Absent", "Sparse", "Moderate", "Frequent")) - 1L)
stopifnot("Braak, Thal and CERAD are complete and on their ordered scales" =
            !anyNA(stage_tbl[c("braak_num", "thal_num", "cerad_num")]) && nrow(stage_tbl) == 84L)
STAGE_SENS <- tribble(~region, ~marker, ~stage,
                      "DFC", "AT8 (pTau)", "Braak", "HIP", "AT8 (pTau)", "Braak",
                      "MTG", "6E10 (Aβ)", "Thal", "MTG", "6E10 (Aβ)", "CERAD")
stopifnot("conventional-stage sensitivities limited to DFC/HIP AT8 x Braak and MTG 6E10 x Thal/CERAD" =
            nrow(STAGE_SENS) == 4L && all(STAGE_SENS$stage[STAGE_SENS$marker == "6E10 (Aβ)"] %in% c("Thal", "CERAD")) &&
            all(STAGE_SENS$region[STAGE_SENS$stage %in% c("Thal", "CERAD")] == "MTG"))

# HIP x Braak
hip_bk <- hip %>% left_join(stage_tbl %>% select(donor_id, braak_num), by = "donor_id") %>%
  mutate(bkz = (braak_num - mean(braak_num[!duplicated(donor_id)])) / sd(braak_num[!duplicated(donor_id)]))
hip_braak <- hip_omni(hip_bk, "bkz")
hip_bk_w <- hip_bk %>% select(donor_id, compartment, clr, bkz) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = clr)
hip_braak_slopes <- setNames(map_dbl(HIP_COMP, ~ unname(coef(lm(hip_bk_w[[.x]] ~ hip_bk_w$bkz))[2])), HIP_COMP)

# MTG 6E10 x Thal / CERAD, on the Figure 5A equal-layer cumulative curve
ab_cum <- mk_cum %>% filter(brain_region == "MTG", marker == "6E10 (Aβ)")
stage_cum <- function(stage) {
  st <- stage_tbl %>% transmute(donor_id, s = .data[[stage]]) %>% mutate(gz = zstd(s)) %>% select(donor_id, gz)
  cum_test(ab_cum %>% select(-gz) %>% left_join(st, by = "donor_id"))
}
ab_stage <- bind_rows(cum_test(ab_cum) %>% mutate(index = "Global pTau (Figure 5A)"),
                      stage_cum("thal_num") %>% mutate(index = "Thal phase"),
                      stage_cum("cerad_num") %>% mutate(index = "CERAD score"))
ab_pattern <- ab_stage %>% group_by(index) %>% summarise(p = first(p), n = first(n), std = list(std), .groups = "drop")
same_sign <- function(v) sum(sign(v) == sign(ab_pattern$std[[which(ab_pattern$index == "Global pTau (Figure 5A)")]]))
ast <- function(ix, col = "p") ab_pattern[[col]][ab_pattern$index == ix]
tibble(Sensitivity = c("HIP AT8 compartment profile × Braak (ordered)", paste("MTG 6E10 depth profile ×", c("Thal phase", "CERAD score"))),
       Donors = c(hip_res$n, ast("Thal phase", "n"), ast("CERAD score", "n")),
       `Omnibus F (df)` = c(sprintf("%.2f (6, %d)", hip_braak$F, hip_braak$df2), map_chr(c("Thal phase", "CERAD score"), function(ix) {
         x <- ab_stage %>% filter(index == ix); sprintf("%.2f (4, %d)", x$F[1], x$df2[1]) })),
       p = format(c(hip_braak$p, ast("Thal phase"), ast("CERAD score")), digits = 2),
       `Direction vs Global pTau` = c(
         sprintf("%d of 7 compartment slopes same sign (EC %+.2f, CA3 %+.2f, CA4 %+.2f)",
                 sum(sign(hip_braak_slopes) == sign(hip_slopes)), hip_braak_slopes[["EC"]], hip_braak_slopes[["CA3"]], hip_braak_slopes[["CA4"]]),
         map_chr(c("Thal phase", "CERAD score"), ~ sprintf("%d of 4 boundary slopes same sign (%s)", same_sign(ab_pattern$std[[which(ab_pattern$index == .x)]]),
                                                            paste(sprintf("%+.2f", ab_pattern$std[[which(ab_pattern$index == .x)]]), collapse = " "))))) %>%
  show_table(caption = sprintf("Conventional-stage sensitivities (CR1 donor-cluster Wald, as in the primary analyses). MTG 6E10 Global pTau pattern for reference: %s (standardized slopes at the four deep → superficial boundaries). Stages are pathology-derived categories of the same lesion type, so these are convergent sensitivities, not independent validation.",
                               paste(sprintf("%+.2f", ab_pattern$std[[which(ab_pattern$index == "Global pTau (Figure 5A)")]]), collapse = " ")))
write_csv(bind_rows(tibble(analysis = "HIP AT8 x Braak", term = HIP_COMP, value = hip_braak_slopes, p = hip_braak$p),
                    ab_stage %>% transmute(analysis = paste("MTG 6E10 x", index), term = CUM_LAB[k], value = std, p)),
          file.path(LAM_TAB_DIR, "stage_sensitivities.csv"))
```

**Reading.**

- **HIP × Braak:** the compartment profile changes with Braak stage (p
  `r format(hip_braak$p, digits = 2)`), with `r sum(sign(hip_braak_slopes) == sign(hip_slopes))` of 7
  compartment slopes in the Global pTau direction. A convergent tau-stage sensitivity.
- **MTG 6E10 × Thal:** p `r format(ast("Thal phase"), digits = 2)`; × **CERAD:** p
  `r format(ast("CERAD score"), digits = 2)`; `r same_sign(ab_pattern$std[[which(ab_pattern$index == "Thal phase")]])`
  and `r same_sign(ab_pattern$std[[which(ab_pattern$index == "CERAD score")]])` of 4 boundary slopes
  share the Global pTau sign. These say whether the MTG amyloid depth phenotype is organized along
  conventional amyloid staging; they are not used to rank markers.


### 7.12 What the laminar and anatomical extension answers

1. **How much does the regional value leave out?** **A small relative-depth component.**
   - **Scale versus distribution.** The regional summary captures the dominant scale component of
     the layer measurements (`r percent(mean(lam_var_tbl[["Donor (burden) share"]]), 1)` of log
     layer-AT8 variance); a relative-depth component of
     `r percent(mean(lam_var_tbl[["Donor × layer (profile + error) share"]]), 1)` remains. Because
     grey matter is the area-weighted aggregate of the same layers, this is
     a decomposition of correlated measurements, not a biological variance partition.
   - **The remainder is not only noise.** It changes with progression (DFC), shows weak but
     detectable MTG–DFC concordance even after progression is removed (Supplementary Figure S4B),
     and varies among donors at comparable Global pTau (Figure 4A).
2. **Does progression alter how relative AT8 is distributed across cortical depth?** **Yes in
   DFC; weakly and fragilely in MTG; and the two regions differ.**
   - **DFC:** AT8 increases with progression in every layer, but disproportionately more in
     deeper layers (absolute L1 `r lar_fmt("DFC", "Layer1")` vs L4 `r lar_fmt("DFC", "Layer4")`
     log2 per SD), producing a relatively deeper-weighted profile (q `r format(lb("DFC"), digits = 2)`).
     Robust to severe-donor exclusion, every leave-one-out and every representation, with a
     convergent Braak-stage sensitivity (p `r format(lam_braak_lin$p, digits = 2)`).
   - **MTG:** same direction, at the margin for the equal-layer concentration profile (q
     `r format(lb("MTG"), digits = 2)`; cumulative p `r format(lr("MTG", "cum_p"), digits = 2)`). The
     area-weighted section contribution, a different estimand, is not supported (p
     `r format(lr("MTG", "cum_A_p"), digits = 2)`); MTG's changing layer geometry contributes to the gap.
   - **Direct comparison:** region × layer × Global pTau p `r format(ldir("p"), digits = 2)`.
   - **Global vs local:** global stage and local burden index the change equally well.
3. **Is it selective to AT8?** **Comparatively, in DFC; MTG shows a broader, geometry-sensitive
   pattern.** Among the six measured QNP families, only AT8 showed FDR-supported
   progression-associated cortical-depth reorganization in DFC (no between-marker interaction
   model, so not formal tau specificity). In MTG several
   do (`r paste(mk_sig("MTG"), collapse = ", ")`). Of these, 6E10 and GFAP persist in the
   area-weighted section contribution and also differ from DFC by direct test; IBA1 does not
   persist with area, and neither IBA1 nor NeuN is shown to differ from DFC. AT8's depth change
   differs between regions (q `r format(lmd("AT8 (pTau)"), digits = 2)`).
4. **Does a comparable internal redistribution exist outside the neocortex?** **Yes, in the
   hippocampus.** Absolute AT8 rises in every compartment; within the normalized
   compartment-mean profile, EC/Sub/CA1 become relatively lower and CA3/CA4 relatively higher at
   higher progression (p `r format(hip_res$p, digits = 2)`), beyond
   each donor's overall hippocampal AT8 level, in each hemisphere alone. MEC has no internal subdivision beyond
   hemisphere.
5. **Does AT8–NeuN covariation differ by depth?** **Yes in MTG, not demonstrably in DFC.** MTG's
   L2 and deep-layer associations are stable without the severely affected donors; only L1 moves.
   None of this establishes neuronal loss, and positive deep-layer associations are neither
   protective nor evidence of neuron preservation.
6. **Does the laminar profile add cognitive information?** **No robust, generalizable information
   at n = 69.** Held-out ΔR² ranges `r sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", min(lam_D$cv_dr2), max(lam_D$cv_dr2))`;
   every DFC cell is negative; no cell survives FDR.
7. **Do hippocampal burden or its internal profile add cognitive information?** **Not as a burden
   term or an arbitrary 6-df profile** (Section 7.10, Figure 6; no increment survives the 12-test
   FDR). A single pathology-defined profile-advancement score is tested in Section 9.3.

**What the released data cannot answer.** The layer and subfield tables are aggregate section
summaries. They preserve no pial-to-white-matter geometry, so none of these results shows local
propagation, spread between layers, a cortical-column trajectory or the order in which layers
accumulate pathology. The local cumulative measure (along normalized pial-to-white-matter
trajectories, averaged across tissue) would need the images, or the MTG MERFISH depth coordinates
for the molecular side (Section 7.9).

**Prior-work boundary and redundancy.**

- **Not reproduced.** This section does not repeat SEA-AD's layer-specific microglia–amyloid
  analysis in MTG, and runs no marker × layer × cognition model.
- **Largely expected.** Concentration of neurofibrillary pathology in pyramidal-neuron-rich layers
  at advanced stages, layer-dependent neuronal vulnerability, and the hippocampal EC → CA1/Sub →
  CA3/CA4 staging sequence are classical neuropathology. The directions found here are expected.
- **What this section adds:**
  - a quantified scale-versus-distribution split in the same donors, for cortex and hippocampus;
  - a direct test that DFC and MTG differ in progression-associated depth redistribution;
  - evidence that DFC's redistribution is comparatively selective to AT8 among six QNP families, with
    direct regional tests for every marker;
  - an explicit absolute-versus-relative separation, so relative depletion is never read as decline;
  - a fold-safe, FDR-controlled null for the laminar profile's cognitive increment.

**Morphology bridge.** Cortical thickness does not measure any histological layer, and no
morphology analysis is started here. The results set four expectations:

- **Burden first.** Morphology models should keep regional AT8 burden (or local pTau CPS) as the
  primary pathology term; any depth term is a prespecified secondary block.
- **DFC is the region where depth organization changes.** The DFC test is whether, at fixed
  regional burden, a deeper-weighted AT8 profile goes with more local cortical thinning or
  deformation. MTG is the comparison region.
- **MTG layer geometry moves with disease.** The classifier-derived MTG layer-area fractions
  change with progression on every stain slide (L3 smaller, L4 larger; Supplementary Figure S5A).
  Whether that is anatomical remodeling or altered NeuN-guided boundary assignment is a direct
  morphology question, and any analysis that relies on layer annotations must expect it.
- **No cognitive contribution beyond burden was shown.** Any morphology–cognition model should not
  expect the laminar profile to add information at n ≈ 69, and should test any such term as one
  prespecified block under the same FDR and cross-validation discipline.

**Carried forward:** regional burden *B*; the 4-contrast AT8 laminar block (clr, L1–L4); the
cumulative normalized layer-mean curve as a descriptive display; the DFC layer × progression
slopes; the HIP compartment × progression slopes; the MTG NeuN laminar-shift contrast; and the
severely affected exclusion as the standard NeuN sensitivity.
